auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDINGS a sibling auditor needs.

1. THREE OF MY SIX FLAGS ARE INERT, AND FOUR OF SIX SHARE ONE BUG. `--agents` and `--forecast-agents` are not read by their handlers at all; `--capacity-label` is read but its equals-form is dropped; `--robot-min-confidence` is read by nobody. Only `--capacity-label` (space form) has any effect in Rust. The value of this group is mostly in the shared parsing layer, not in six separate algorithms.

2. THE `--robot-forecast` COMMAND IS MORE BROKEN THAN ITS FLAGS. `run_robot_forecast` (main.rs:5964) is a completely different program from Go's: Go derives targets from the issue set and only touches `loader.LoadSprints` when `--forecast-sprint` is non-blank, whereas Rust makes an active sprint mandatory (main.rs:5977-5999) and exits 1. So EVERY `--robot-forecast` invocation fails on this repo regardless of my flags (`--robot-forecast all` alone: go=0/rust=1). Fixing `--forecast-label`/`--forecast-agents`/`--forecast-sprint` means rewriting this handler and porting pkg/analysis/eta.go (298 lines) — not patching three flags. `bv_core::sprint::estimate_forecast` (crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs:646) is a different heuristic and must not be reused as-is.

3. `--robot-capacity` HAS NO ETA ENGINE TO CALL. Go's capacity numbers all come from `analysis.EstimateETAForIssue`, which is unported. Neither `EstimateETAForIssue` nor `Analyzer.IsCandidate` (graph.go:1358) nor `Analyzer.Readiness()` (graph.go:1352) exists in bv-analysis. `ReadinessIndex` DOES exist at crates/bv-correlation/src/readiness.rs:79, and crates/bv-analysis/Cargo.toml:16 already depends on bv-correlation, so the readiness half is reachable without a new crate edge; the ETA half is greenfield. Until the ETA port lands, `--agents` and `--capacity-label` cannot produce correct numbers no matter how they are parsed.

4. GO'S `--agents` AND `--forecast-agents` ARE ASYMMETRIC — DO NOT "UNIFY" THEM. Capacity's `--agents` is applied only to `effectiveMinutes` via INTEGER division (robot_registry.go:3620) and never touches total/serial/parallel; forecast's `--forecast-agents` is passed straight into every `EstimateETAForIssue` call. Also note capacity hardcodes `agents=1` in both of its own ETA calls (:3577, :3603). A shared "agents" helper that feeds the ETA engine would produce wrong capacity numbers. Verified outputs: agents=3 -> 0.23541666, agents=4 (label tui) -> 0.18125, both consistent with truncating integer division.

5. GO USES TRIMMED-BLANK-AS-ABSENT THROUGHOUT. `strings.TrimSpace(*cfg.X) != ""` guards the label filters, the sprint filter, the min-confidence filter, and both `filters`/`Label` echoes. Rust's handlers use `.filter(|v| !v.is_empty())`, which treats `"   "` as a real label. Demonstrated: Go with `--capacity-label "  "` emits no `label` key and reports 3 open issues.

6. ARGUMENT EXTRACTION IS AD-HOC AND SYSTEMATICALLY INCOMPLETE. The pattern `args.iter().position(|a| a == "--flag").and_then(|i| args.get(i+1))` (main.rs:5966, 6021, 4835, 4839, and ~50 more sites) breaks on three things: the `--flag=value` form, a missing value, and float/int type errors. A single shared `flag_value(args, name) -> Result<Option<String>, ArgError>` plus a per-flag typed parse, run before dispatch, would fix `--agents`, `--forecast-agents`, `--capacity-label`, `--forecast-sprint`, `--forecast-label`, and `--robot-min-confidence` in one move and prevent recurrence. crates/bv/src/flags.rs already has a full typed registry (STRING_FLAGS / INT_FLAGS / FLOAT_FLAGS near flags.rs:1600-1650) that this extractor should read from.

7. argv.rs HAS A GLOBAL PANIC, NOT A FLAG BUG. crates/bv/src/argv.rs:37 evaluates `arg[1..].find('=').unwrap_or(arg.len() - 1)` one line BEFORE the `arg.len() > 2` guard that is supposed to make the slice safe. Any empty-string argv token panics: `bvr ""` -> exit 101, `bv ""` -> exit 1 with `unknown command "" for "bv"`. Reachable from any of my string flags with an empty value (`--capacity-label ""`, `--forecast-sprint ""`). This is the highest-severity item in my group because it is one line and it affects the whole binary.

8. ONE SHARED "Try:" HINT GAP. All five of my modifiers trip the modifier-requires path, where Go appends a per-modifier recovery example (main.go:236-244 `formatModifierRecoveryExamples`, mapping at main.go:299-301) to the error and Rust instead prints a fixed `Usage: bvr --robot-help` line (main.rs:48). Exit code and first stderr line match; only line 2 differs. This is one function to add in validation.rs, and it will also fix roughly 40 other modifiers owned by other groups.

9. PRE-EXISTING, FLAG-INDEPENDENT, DO NOT DOUBLE-REPORT. (a) The 9 `.status.*.ms` timing leaves in robot-priority output appear on a bare `./scripts/diff_robot.sh --robot-priority` — Rust emits wall-clock metric timings that Go omits; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH does not pin them. (b) Rust's capacity payload carries a Rust-only `usage_hints` array whose text literally says "This is a simplified capacity snapshot... see plan doc §11" — it will disappear when the handler is rewritten. (c) Neither repo has a `.beads/sprints.jsonl`, so `--robot-burndown` and any positive `--forecast-sprint` case are untestable here; the sprint file path is already correct on both sides (pkg/loader/sprint.go:21 vs crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs:1234), so the sprint lookup itself is not a gap — only the control flow around it is.

10. AUDIT METHOD NOTE. diff_robot.sh reports stdout leaves plus both exit codes, and separately diffs the first 20 stderr lines — so "STDOUT: byte-identical" with matching exits does NOT mean parity when a "### STDERR DIFFERS" block follows. For `--forecast-sprint` and for the empty/modifier-only invocations, the flag's entire observable effect is on stderr. Read the stderr block, not just the stdout verdict.
verifierSummary:
ALL SIX GAPS ARE REAL AND NONE IS AT PARITY — I reproduced every one with my own diff_robot.sh runs. I am marking refuted=true on all six for a different reason than the schema implies: the implementation advice is materially wrong on five of them, and materially wrong in one sub-item on the sixth. Read every correctedVerdict as "gap" — do not read refuted=true as "already handled."

THE DECISIVE FINDING: the previous audit's biggest structural claim is false. It asserts (groupNotes #3, and implementation steps for --agents/--forecast-label/--capacity-label) that `EstimateETAForIssue` is "greenfield" / unported and that the implementer must first port pkg/analysis/eta.go (298 lines, 8 funcs). That port ALREADY EXISTS. crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs contains `estimate_eta_for_issue` (:325), `estimate_complexity_minutes` (:400), `estimate_velocity_minutes_per_day` (:460), `velocity_minutes_per_day_for_label` (:514), `has_label` (:570), `estimate_eta_confidence` (:583), `compute_median_estimated_minutes` (:609), `duration_days` (:630) — all eight of Go's eta.go funcs, under a header reading "ETA estimation for a single issue (Go: `ETAEstimate`)". `ETAEstimate` (:278), `ForecastSummary` (:300) and `ForecastOutput` (:310) already carry Go's exact JSON tags. Better still, TWO ready-made Go-shaped builders already exist and have ZERO non-test callers: `compute_forecast_output(issues, sprint_bead_ids, label_filter, agents, now) -> ForecastOutput` (:685), which already takes label_filter AND agents AND sprint_bead_ids and already implements the filters map and the >1 summary rule, and `calculate_capacity(issues, agents, label_filter) -> CapacityOutput` (:816), which already has Go's exact `CapacityOutput` schema struct (:783), already does the two-pass label-then-open filter, and already does Go's INTEGER division `serial_minutes + parallel_minutes / agents` (:955-957). Both are unit-tested (e.g. `capacity_with_label_filter` :1780, `capacity_estimated_days_with_agents` :1830, `compute_forecast_output_with_label_filter` :1641). I verified crates/bv/Cargo.toml:14 depends on bv-core, and grepped every `bv_core::sprint::` call site in main.rs: the CLI uses only `load_sprints`, `calculate_burndown` and the legacy `estimate_forecast` (:6002) — never `compute_forecast_output` or `calculate_capacity`. The real task is WIRING (~40 lines), not porting. The audit's related pointer is also wrong: `compute_median_estimated_minutes` is at crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs:609, not crates/bv-analysis/src/impact.rs:494.

SECOND AUDIT ERROR: groupNotes #6 tells the implementer that "crates/bv/src/flags.rs already has a full typed registry (STRING_FLAGS / INT_FLAGS / FLOAT_FLAGS near flags.rs:1600-1650)". No such arrays exist. There is ONE array, `MODIFIER_FLAGS: &[FlagDef]` (flags.rs:1543), with kind carried in the `FlagKind` enum (flags.rs:19: Bool/Str/Int/Float/RepeatableStr) and built by the `s()`/`i()`/`b()`/`f2()` const helpers. All six flags are already correctly typed there (flags.rs:1623-1631). The audit's proposed shared-extractor idea is sound; only the symbol names are wrong.

WHAT THE AUDIT GOT RIGHT AND I CONFIRMED: the --capacity-label closed-filter bug (9 vs 2); equals-form blindness (Rust uses `position(|a| a == flag)` at main.rs:5967/6022 only); the argv.rs empty-token panic (real, global, exit 101 vs Go's exit 1 `unknown command "" for "bv"`, reproducible with a bare `bvr ""`); Go's `> 0` / `TrimSpace != ""` fallbacks for agents and labels; the capacity/forecast integer-division and fallback-to-1 semantics; the `Try:` recovery-hint gap; the pre-existing 9 `.status.*.ms` leaves (do not attribute to any flag); and that neither repo has .beads/sprints.jsonl so --forecast-sprint is only testable on its not-found path.

WHAT THE AUDIT GOT WRONG, CORRECTED: (1) Go's handlers apply an `analyzer.IsCandidate(issue.ID)` pre-filter the audit never mentions (robot_registry.go:3540 capacity, :1467 forecast) — material, since `--robot-capacity --label tui` gives Go open_issue_count=2 via that path. (2) `run_robot_priority`'s high_confidence tally reads `r["impact_score"] > 0.5` (main.rs:5038); Go counts `rec.Confidence >= 0.7`, so the fix must change the FIELD as well as the threshold — the audit's "change 0.5 to 0.7" alone still ships a wrong count. (3) Go's min-confidence confidences are [0.375, 0.375], not [0.8, 0.375], and at threshold 0.5 Go drops BOTH (count 0); the audit's evidence numbers are wrong. (4) Go's stderr for `abc` is `invalid argument "abc" for "--robot-min-confidence" flag: strconv.ParseFloat: parsing "abc": invalid syntax`, not the message quoted. (5) forecast payload sizes are 2550B/2542B, not 2559B/2551B (immaterial). (6) the panic is argv.rs:38 with the guard on :39, not :37/:38 (immaterial).

SCOPE NOTE: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md:645-649 records capacity ("basic snapshot") and forecast ("velocity-target-only") as deliberate, documented scope cuts, and the Rust-only `usage_hints` array is the marker. So the schema divergence itself is planned work, not a surprise — but the flag-level bugs layered on top (ignored label, ignored agents, mandatory sprint, missing closed/tombstone filter) are NOT covered by that cut and remain real.

RESIDUAL FIDELITY GAPS the next agent must not miss, all inside the already-written bv-core code rather than requiring a rewrite: (a) `calculate_capacity` and `compute_forecast_output` both hardcode `critical_path_depth = 0.0` into `estimate_eta_for_issue`, while Go passes real graph stats (`stats.GetCriticalPathScore(issue.ID)`, pkg/analysis/eta.go:130) — thread `critical_path_score` (already available as `Option<BTreeMap<String,f64>>` at crates/bv-analysis/src/analyzer.rs:208) or total_minutes/serial_minutes will not match Go's 207/66. (b) `compute_forecast_output` sets `filters["sprint"]` from `ids.iter().next()` on the bead-id HashSet (sprint.rs:756-762) — a non-deterministic BEAD id where Go emits the SPRINT id. (c) `compute_forecast_output` filters `status.is_closed()` unconditionally, but Go applies that skip only in the `all` branch (robot_registry.go:1514-1516), and it does not model the single-id `Issue not found in selected forecast scope: <id>` exit-1 path. (d) `calculate_capacity`'s open pass lacks Go's tombstone exclusion (`Status::Tombstone` exists at crates/bv-core/src/model.rs:96; unreachable on this corpus since tombstones=0, but wrong in general).

UNVERIFIED: I could not test a positive `--forecast-sprint` case or `--robot-burndown` at all, because neither repo has `.beads/sprints.jsonl`; the sprint load path itself is already correct on both sides (Go pkg/loader/sprint.go:21 vs Rust sprint.rs:1234). I also did not attempt to compute what `calculate_capacity` would actually emit on this corpus (that would have required writing code, which is out of bounds here), so point (a) above is a code-level inference, not a measured diff.

flags.goBehavior: robot_registry.go:3543-3552 filters targetIssues by exact label match (`for _, label := range issue.Labels { if label == *cfg.CapacityLabel }`) only when `strings.TrimSpace(*cfg.CapacityLabel) != ""`. robot_registry.go:3683-3685 sets `output.Label` under the same blank check, and the field is `json:"label,omitempty"`. Critically, the label filter selects the *candidate pool*, and open-status filtering is a SEPARATE later pass: robot_registry.go:3558-3563 builds `openIssues` from targetIssues with `!issue.Status.IsClosed() && !issue.Status.IsTombstone()`. So label and open-status compose; a label match does not bypass the closed filter.

flags.implementation: Do NOT hand-roll a new capacity handler. In `run_robot_capacity` (crates/bv/src/main.rs:6019) delete the bespoke `filtered` computation and the `capacity{...}`/`usage_hints` payload (main.rs:6032-6068) and instead: (a) parse `--agents` and `--capacity-label` with one `=`-aware extractor that errors on a missing value; (b) map a blank/blank-only label to `None` (Go guards on `strings.TrimSpace(...) != ""`); (c) call `bv_core::sprint::calculate_capacity(&issues, agents, label_opt)` -- it already clamps agents to >=1 and emits Go's schema; (d) spread the serialized `CapacityOutput` leaves at the top level alongside the envelope from `full_envelope_for`. Two residual fidelity gaps remain INSIDE the already-written function and must be fixed there, not by rewriting: (1) sprint.rs:850/930 hardcode `estimate_complexity_minutes(iss, median_minutes, 0.0)` whereas Go's `EstimateETAForIssue` uses `stats.GetCriticalPathScore(issue.ID)` (pkg/analysis/eta.go:130) -- thread `critical_path_score` (available as `Option<BTreeMap<String,f64>>` at crates/bv-analysis/src/analyzer.rs:208) through, or total_minutes/serial_minutes will not match Go's 207/66; (2) the open pass (sprint.rs:842) lacks Go's tombstone exclusion (`!IsTombstone()`, Rust has `Status::Tombstone` at model.rs:96) and the target pass lacks `analyzer.IsCandidate`. Then fix crates/bv/src/argv.rs:38 by hoisting the length guard so an empty argv token cannot panic.

Reproduced: `./scripts/diff_robot.sh --robot-capacity --capacity-label tui` -> go open_issue_count=2, rust capacity.open_count=9; corpus confirms 9 issues carry "tui" (7 closed, 2 open), so the Rust label branch admits closed work. `--capacity-label=tui` -> rust label_filter=null, open=3 (equals form dropped). `--capacity-label` with no value -> go exit 1 'flag needs an argument', rust exit 0. `--capacity-label ""` -> go exit 0, rust exit 101 panic at crates/bv/src/argv.rs:38:32. The audit's goBehavior text is accurate except that it omits Go's `analyzer.IsCandidate(issue.ID)` pre-filter (robot_registry.go:3540-3542), which is load-bearing: I confirmed `--robot-capacity --label tui` yields go open_issue_count=2. THE ADVICE IS WRONG WHERE IT MATTERS MOST: it says 'This requires the EstimateETAForIssue port (see --agents entry)' and tells the implementer to replace the capacity payload by hand. `bv_core::sprint::calculate_capacity` (crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs:816) ALREADY EXISTS and already returns a `CapacityOutput` struct (sprint.rs:783) whose serde field names are Go's exact schema (agents, label omitempty, open_issue_count, total_minutes, total_days, serial_minutes, parallel_minutes, parallelizable_pct, estimated_days, critical_path_length, critical_path omitempty, actionable_count, actionable omitempty, bottlenecks omitempty), including the two-pass label-then-open filter and Go's INTEGER division `serial_minutes + parallel_minutes / agents` (sprint.rs:956). It has unit tests incl. `capacity_with_label_filter` (sprint.rs:1780) and `capacity_estimated_days_with_agents` (sprint.rs:1830). It has ZERO non-test callers. Also note the bespoke `capacity{...}` blob + `usage_hints` IS a documented scope cut (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md:645-649: 'Documented scope cuts vs Go: ... capacity basic snapshot'), so the schema divergence is planned, not an oversight -- but the label filter bug on top of it is not.

flags.goBehavior: robot_registry.go:3570-3572: `agents := 1; if cfg.CapacityAgents != nil && *cfg.CapacityAgents > 0 { agents = *cfg.CapacityAgents }` — so 0 and any negative value silently fall back to 1. The variable is used in exactly ONE place, robot_registry.go:3620: `effectiveMinutes := serialMinutes + parallelMinutes/agents`. That division is Go INTEGER division (both operands are `int`), and only `estimatedDays` (:3621) is derived from it. `totalMinutes` (:3576-3581) and `serialMinutes` (:3602-3607) both hardcode `agents=1` in their `EstimateETAForIssue` calls (:3577, :3603), so `--agents` never changes total_minutes/total_days/serial_minutes/parallel_minutes/parallelizable_pct. The value is also echoed as the top-level `agents` field (:3670).

flags.verifierReason: THE GAP IS REAL AND REPRODUCED. `grep -n 'a == "--agents"' crates/bv/src/*.rs` returns nothing -- the flag is never parsed in the Rust binary, and `--robot-capacity --agents 3` produces Rust output byte-identical to the bare `--robot-capacity` run. Go oracle confirms the semantics: agents=0 -> 1, agents=-1 -> 1, agents=3 -> 3 with estimated_days 0.23541666666666666 (= 66 + 141/3 = 113, 113/480), agents=4 -> 0.21041666666666667 (= 66 + 141/4 = 101). `--agents abc` -> go exit 1 'invalid argument "abc" for "--agents" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "abc": invalid syntax', rust exit 0. THE ADVICE IS MATERIALLY WRONG: it says the ETA half is greenfield and must be ported, and hand-writes the `effective_minutes` math. Both are already in `bv_core::sprint::calculate_capacity` (crates/bv-core/src/sprint.rs:816): the `let agents = agents.max(1)` clamp is at sprint.rs:813 and the Go integer-division `let effective_minutes = serial_minutes + parallel_minutes / agents; let estimated_days = effective_minutes as f64 / WORKDAY_HOURS;` is at sprint.rs:955-957, with `const WORKDAY_HOURS: f64 = 60.0 * 8.0` at sprint.rs:25. STRUCTURAL FINDINGS A SIBLING AUDITOR SHOULD KNOW

1. All five handlers in this group are placeholders, not partial ports. None of the three file/relation commands emit any of the data the flags are supposed to slice:

It does NOT record the JSON field-name/shape difference as a cut, and AGENTS.md's contract item 1 demands "field-for-field identical" schemas and says "When in doubt, the Go code wins over this document." So the shape mismatch is a real gap, not an accepted cut. (4) FlagKind is decorative — confirmed: its only consumer is print_robot_help() at main.rs:6949-6952, which iterates ROBOT_PRIMARIES; these 6 are modifiers and never appear there.

(A) --file-beads-limit: the suggested `limit.clamp(0, 20_max)` is WRONG — Go has no upper clamp (robot_registry.go:3143-3150). 20 is only the flag DEFAULT; `--file-beads-limit 100` is honoured verbatim. ONE ROOT-CAUSE ERROR that would misdirect the implementer (groupNote #1, not a flag verdict):
The audit hypothesises "load_correlation_report yielding commits with no files". That is WRONG. correlate() faithfully copies `files: commit.files.clone()` (correlator.rs:141 and the temporal branch ~line 200), and walk_commits correctly parses `git log --name-only` (correlator.rs:42-90) — I confirmed raw git log returns proper file lists. The real cause is that the Rust correlation report is EMPTY on this repo. All 4 bead IDs Go reports as correlated to crates/bv/src/main.rs return "Bead not found in correlation report" from `bvr --robot-explain-correlation <sha>:<bead>`. Consequently Rust's network has 43 edges that are ALL `dependency` — zero shared_commit, zero shared_file. So --robot-file-beads/hotspots/file-relations are empty because there are zero correlations, not because a `files` field was stripped. Fixing "commits have no files" would be a dead end; the explicit-ID signal never fires on these commit subjects and the temporal signal requires an exact assignee-to-git-author match (a documented plan cut). auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDINGS A SIBLING AUDITOR SHOULD KNOW

1. `crates/bv/src/validation.rs:32-40` (`Presence::from_args`) inserts EVERY argv token into the present set after stripping a leading `--` and truncating at `=`. That means flag VALUES and bare POSITIONALS register as "present flags". Consequences observed: `bv robot-search "login oauth" --json` satisfies `has("robot-search")` via the positional and then fails MODIFIER_REQUIRES instead of being rewritten into `--search <query> --robot-search`; `--format=bogus` is "present" so validation fires but the value lookup at main.rs:181-185 fails. This is a cross-cutting bug affecting every flag group, not just search.

2. THE RUST `bv-search` LIBRARY IS ALREADY A NEAR-COMPLETE PORT — only the CLI wiring in `crates/bv/src/main.rs:5471` (`run_robot_search`) is missing. These already exist and are currently UNUSED by any CLI path: `bv_search::query::issue_document` (query.rs:184, = Go's IssueDocument with id x3 / title x2 / labels / desc), `bv_search::query::short_query_lexical_boost` (query.rs:138, = the +0.35 boost), `bv_search::query::is_short_query` (query.rs:49), `bv_search::query::hybrid_candidate_limit` (query.rs:97), `bv_search::index_sync::{default_index_path, load_or_new, sync_index}` (index_sync.rs:33/44/77), and `bv_search::vector_index::VectorIndex::{load, save, search_top_k}`. The 5 hybrid preset tables are also an exact value-for-value port (bv-search/src/hybrid.rs:20-70 vs Go pkg/search/presets.go). The implementer should wire these up rather than re-derive them.

3. GO SEARCH OUTPUT TOP-LEVEL KEY ORDER (observed, must match byte-for-byte): `generated_at, data_hash, output_format, version, source_path, source_kind, source_authority, authority_hash, scope_hash, index_data_hash, candidate_hash, ranking_hash, ranking_time, query, provider, dim, index_path, index, loaded, limit, mode, preset, weights, results, usage_hints`. Rust currently emits `..., scope_hash, query, mode, preset, limit, results, usage_hints` — note `limit` is misplaced (Go puts it before `mode`).

4. `component_scores` is a Go `map[string]float64`, so `encoding/json` emits its keys SORTED: `impact, pagerank, priority, recency, status`. Rust's `run_robot_search` serializes the `ComponentScores` STRUCT (hybrid.rs:88) and emits declaration order `pagerank, status, impact, priority, recency`. `HybridResult` (hybrid.rs:169) already uses a `BTreeMap` and gets this right — switch to it.

5. `robotSearchResult.TextScore` has `json:"text_score,omitempty"` in Go (search_output.go:21), so a 0 text score is OMITTED. Rust always emits `"text_score": 0`.

6. `--search` WITHOUT `--robot-search` IS THE TUI IN RUST. `run_robot_search` is only reached from `presence.has("robot-search")` (main.rs:297). Go, by contrast, runs the whole pipeline whenever `*semanticQuery != ""` (main.go:2815) and prints a human table to stdout. I accidentally triggered the TUI while probing this and had to kill it — do not run a bare `--search` in diff_robot.sh; always pair it with `--robot-search` or another non-interactive flag.

7. `--as-of` is silently ignored by the Rust search path: `run_robot_search` calls `load_issues_auto(&cwd, None)` (main.rs:5502), so `.as_of` / `.as_of_commit` are absent and `index_path` never gets the `historical-<sha>-` prefix. Likely a shared gap with whoever owns `--as-of`.

8. `--robot-by-label` / `--robot-by-assignee` on the Rust search path produce EMPTY stdout (exit nonzero) even though Go ignores them there. Not in my group, but a sibling should confirm.

9. ENV VARS READ BY GO BUT BY NO RUST CODE PATH: BV_SEARCH_MODE, BV_SEARCH_PRESET, BV_SEARCH_WEIGHTS (pkg/search/config.go:58-60), BV_OUTPUT_FORMAT, TOON_DEFAULT_FORMAT, TOON_KEY_FOLDING, TOON_INDENT, TOON_STATS. Rust mentions BV_SEARCH_MODE/BV_SEARCH_PRESET only in help text (flags.rs:547/554) and docs (bv-robot/src/docs.rs:241-242) — never as `std::env::var`.

10. Rust's own comments in `run_robot_search` (main.rs:5459-5468) already declare the index sync a deliberate scope cut, and the `usage_hints` string it emits says so ("This build embeds fresh on every call — no persisted vector index yet (see plan doc §11)"). Go's usage_hints are the two jq one-liners (search_output.go via main.go:3013-3016 / 3017-3020). Any port must drop the Rust-specific apology and match Go's, byte for byte.

11. `tru` is not installed in this environment, so no diff_robot.sh run can exercise Go's real TOON encoder. Every `--format toon` test here only exercises the downgrade-to-JSON path. A dedicated environment with `tru` (or TOON_TRU_BIN) is required before `--format` can be called anything but unverified on the toon path.
verifierSummary:
All 9 gap/partial/parity verdicts survived independent re-derivation. I found no flag that is at parity when the audit says it is a gap, and no documented scope cut that rescues one — the only scope cut in COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md §11 (persisted vector index / lexical boost / query adjustment) is already acknowledged by the audit. Every claim I re-tested reproduced on a freshly rebuilt binary. I set refuted=true on 7 of 9 entries: the gap verdicts are right, but the implementation advice is materially wrong or materially incomplete in ways that would ship a NEW divergence if followed verbatim. I set refuted=false on --search-min-score (could not refute; advice correct), --robot-max-results (advice correct and minimal), and --robot-min-confidence (parity confirmed with an added Go-side byte-comparison the audit had not run).

The three most consequential errors found:
(1) --search exact-ID promotion. The advice says "rotate to index 0". Go actually FORCE-INCLUDES the exact match inside SearchTopKWithOptions (pkg/search/vector_index.go:495-567), before the limit truncation, overwriting results[k-1] when the exact ID scores below the cutoff, and matches case-insensitively with a uniqueness guard. Proved with `--search BEADS_VIEWER_RUST-P7-SEARCH-MC8 --search-limit 1`, which returns a 0.365911 result ahead of a 0.410792 one; 25 of 46 beads diverge between promoted and natural top-1.
(2) --search-mode / --search-preset env precedence. The advice's "flag if present else env" is wrong: Go discards inherited env values based on WHICH flags were supplied (a --search-preset flag also discards BV_SEARCH_MODE, and --search-mode text also discards BV_SEARCH_PRESET). Observable: BV_SEARCH_MODE=bogus with any --search-preset exits 0 in Go, not 1. The two error strings also differ (flag path has the `--` prefix, env path does not).
(3) --search-weights validation. The advice omits Go's unknown-key, non-negative, and sum-to-1.0±0.001 checks, so an implementer would accept weights Go rejects.

Also: the advice repeatedly calls `Weights::normalize()`, which does not exist in crates/bv-search/src/hybrid.rs (there is no `impl Weights` block at all), and gives Adjust-before-Normalize where Go does Normalize-then-Adjust (main.go:2938-2939).

Two smaller corrections: --search-limit's parse error must be a GLOBAL flag-parse failure (proved with `--robot-triage --search-limit abc`, which Go rejects before dispatch), and the --format fix must TRIM the value (Go trims; `--format " json "` exits 0 in Go, 2 in Rust) plus rewrite the `--toon`/`--json` aliases, which the audit explicitly mis-reported as "stderr matched" when diff_robot.sh shows a real stderr divergence.

Every measurement below is from that current build. I never ran a bare TUI except under `timeout` with stdin closed, per the read-only and no-bare-TUI rules; no files in either repo were modified.

flags.implementation:
crates/bv/src/main.rs `run_robot_search` (line 5471). Ordered changes:
(1) Document: use `bv_search::query::issue_document(&issue.id, &issue.title, &issue.labels, &issue.description)` (crates/bv-search/src/query.rs:184) instead of `format!("{} {}", issue.title, issue.description)` at main.rs:5521 and 5552.
(2) Port Go's search pipeline order (pkg/search/vector_index.go:495-567), NOT a post-hoc rotate: for each eligible issue compute raw cosine; (a) skip if min_score is Some and score < min_score; (b) add the short-query boost (+0.35 via bv_search::query::short_query_lexical_boost); (c) collect top-k with deterministic tie-break issue_id ascending. Then handle the exact ID inside the collector: prefer an exact-case match, else a case-insensitive match ONLY if exactly one folded match exists; if that result is not already in the list, append it when len < k else overwrite results[k-1]; finally move it to index 0. This is required for byte parity — a rotate-to-0 gives the wrong answer whenever the exact ID scores below the cutoff (demonstrated: p7-search-mc8 @0.3659 beats lw1 @0.4108 at --search-limit 1).
(3) Then, and only then, apply the limit clamp (if limit <= 0 { limit = 10 }) and truncation; in hybrid mode widen the pre-score fetch with bv_search::query::hybrid_candidate_limit(limit, issues.len(), &query) and truncate only AFTER hybrid scoring.
(4) Also gate the human (non-robot) path: when --robot-search is absent, still run the pipeline, print Go's stderr lines ("Building semantic index (%d issues)..." when the index was not loaded, and "Index: +%d ~%d -%d (%d total) -> %s" when !loaded || changed) and Go's `%.4f\t%s\t%s` table to stdout, then exit 0. Required for a bare `bv --search "q"` to match Go.
(5) Emit the missing payload fields in Go's struct order (search_output.go:26-43), including limit BEFORE mode; add index_data_hash (data hash over issuesForSearch), candidate_hash (over selectedIssues), ranking_hash (search_output.go:48-62), ranking_time (hybrid only), provider, dim, index_path, index, loaded. index/loaded/index_path require wiring bv_search::index_sync::{default_index_path, load_or_new, sync_index} + VectorIndex::{load,save}; per the plan doc the current omission is a documented scope cut, so either wire it or keep the omission deliberate — do not fabricate loaded:true.
(6) ranking_hash must be computed AFTER all of mode/preset/weights/min_score/limit/as_of are resolved (it hashes them all), and it must reuse the same analysis.ComputeDataHash the envelope uses, which is currently the v0.20.0 form in crates/bv-core/src/data_hash.rs.

The GAP verdict is confirmed by diff_robot.sh (36 differing leaves: Go emits index_data_hash, candidate_hash, ranking_hash, provider, dim, index_path, index, loaded, ranking_time; Rust emits none, and the result sets and score values differ). But the implementation advice is MATERIALLY WRONG on exact-ID promotion and understates the scope of two other items.

(1) EXACT-ID: the advice says "after sorting, if any result's issue_id == query.trim(), rotate it to index 0 in both the text and hybrid branches (port of search_output.go:176-212)". That is wrong on two counts. (a) Go does the promotion INSIDE idx.SearchTopKWithOptions (pkg/search/vector_index.go:495-567), BEFORE the --search-limit truncation, and it FORCE-INCLUDES the exact result even when it scores below the cutoff — appending it if len(results)<k, else REPLACING results[k-1]. search_output.go:176-212 is only the post-hoc re-rotation and is a no-op given the collector already did it. I proved the force-include with a decisive run: `--search BEADS_VIEWER_RUST-P7-SEARCH-MC8 --search-limit 1` returns beads_viewer_rust-p7-search-mc8 at score 0.365911, while the runner-up beads_viewer_rust-lw1 scores 0.410792 — a strictly LOWER-scoring result is returned. A rotate-to-0 implementation would have returned lw1. I swept all 46 beads and found 25 where the promoted result differs from the natural top-1. (b) The match is case-insensitive with a uniqueness guard (strings.EqualFold, and foldedMatches!=1 disqualifies the folded fallback), not `issue_id == query.trim()`. Uppercased IDs match: `--search BEADS_VIEWER_RUST-LW1` returns beads_viewer_rust-lw1.

(2) The "short-query boost" advice says to "add it to the text score before sorting" — but Go passes the boost as ScoreBoosts into SearchTopKWithOptions, which adds it AFTER the MinScore filter and AFTER the exact-ID bookkeeping (vector_index.go:516-519), and the boost is computed only for eligibleIDs. Rust's in-memory path has no such split, so this is fine in spirit but the ordering matters relative to min-score.

(3) The claim "Move the --search query parse out of the --robot-search gate so `bv --search "q"` runs the pipeline" is correct as a gap statement but is a large behavioural change: Go runs the pipeline whenever *semanticQuery != "" and prints a human `%.4f\t%s\t%s` table to stdout and exits 0. I confirmed Go's bare `--search "login oauth"` exits 0 with a 10-line table, while Rust launches the TUI (timeout 15s, exit 124, stderr "Loaded 46 issues — launching TUI"). The advice does not mention the human-table stdout format or the stderr "Building semantic index..." / "Index: +N ~N -N" lines Go emits on the non-robot path (main.go:2856-2858, 3013-3020).

(4) Point (4) of the advice is accurate about the Go key order (I confirmed: generated_at,data_hash,output_format,version,source_path,source_kind,source_authority,authority_hash,scope_hash,index_data_hash,candidate_hash,ranking_hash[,ranking_time],query,provider,dim,index_path,index,loaded,limit,mode[,preset,weights],results,usage_hints — note limit precedes mode, and ranking_time/preset/weights are omitempty), and it correctly says the index/loaded fields need the persisted index. Verified the bv-search helpers the advice names all exist and are exact ports: query.rs:184 issue_document, query.rs:138 short_query_lexical_boost, query.rs:49 is_short_query, query.rs:97 hybrid_candidate_limit, index_sync.rs:33/44/77, vector_index.rs load/save/search_top_k.

auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDINGS A SIBLING AUDITOR SHOULD KNOW

1. THE SHARED ROOT CAUSE OF EVERY "SHORT FLAG IGNORED" BUG. main() computes `let args = argv::rewrite_args(&raw)` (crates/bv/src/main.rs:22) and threads `args` through dispatch - but the runtime flag *value* readers all re-read the raw process argv with std::env::args(): active_scope_flags (main.rs:655), history_flag_value (main.rs:2205), and the ad-hoc `arg_value` closures (main.rs:5160, main.rs:2209). argv::rewrite_args DOES expand -l/-r/-f (crates/bv/src/argv.rs:10), so the fix is to read the rewritten argv, not to extend the alias table. validation::Presence::from_args already receives the rewritten `args`, which is why --brief's requires-validation is correct while --brief's payload and -l/-r values are not. Whoever owns argv.rs / the other flag groups should fix this in one place rather than per flag.

2. GO'S SCOPING IS APPLIED ONCE, CENTRALLY; RUST'S IS PER-COMMAND. In Go, scopeLoadedIssues (cmd/bv/main.go:4870-4933) runs once at main.go:2786, before the entire robot dispatch, mutating the shared RobotContext. Every handler therefore inherits Issues/CandidateIDs/LabelScope/Recipe/Repo for free. In Rust, scopeLoadedIssues has no analogue: apply_label_scope is called from exactly two sites (main.rs:1111 run_robot_triage, main.rs:5178 run_robot_alerts) and the repo/recipe filters do not exist. The single highest-leverage change for this whole group is to put the scoping step inside load_issues_auto_meta (main.rs:729) and return the candidate set as an extra element, so all ~40 envelope call sites inherit it. Anyone auditing --graph-root, --forecast-label, --capacity-label etc. should check whether those suffer the same "handled in one handler only" shape.

3. THREE SETS, NOT ONE: analysis set, candidate set, and the source hash are independent. Go keeps three things: ctx.Issues (the analysis/graph set), ctx.CandidateIDs (what counts and recommendations are gated on - analyzer.IsCandidate, pkg/analysis/graph.go:1358), and ctx.DataHash. The rules are subtle and worth stating once: --repo sets Candidates to the survivors AND recomputes DataHash; --label sets Candidates to the core set but leaves DataHash alone; --recipe narrows Issues after both and does not touch Candidates or DataHash. Rust's apply_label_scope collapses candidates+analysis into one Vec and throws the candidate set away, which is why the counts differ even where scoping does apply.

4. SOURCE-PROVENANCE BUGS THAT ARE NOT ABOUT MY FLAGS BUT SURFACE WHEN TESTING THEM. Two independent problems, both in how Rust derives envelope provenance: (a) source_meta_for (main.rs:708) re-derives path/kind from cwd instead of using the SourceMeta the loader already computed, so any non-cwd source is mislabelled - this is why the Rust workspace run reported source_kind=jsonl_local with count 46 while reading a 46-issue file that was not the local one. (b) Windows path separators are not normalised when a path arrives from an env var, so source_path comes out as `C:/.../bvdb/.beads\issues.jsonl` instead of all-backslashes. Both will show up in any flag that redirects the source (--db, --workspace, --as-of, BEADS_DB/BEADS_DIR). Fixing source_meta_for's callers is the single change that covers (a) everywhere.

5. ALREADY-AT-PARITY ITEMS IN THIS GROUP, for the record: the `--brief` modifier-requires validation (exit 1 + identical first stderr line, only the trailing hint differs); the envelope's scope object and scope_hash arithmetic for --label/--recipe/--repo (active_scope_flags + label_scope_ids reproduce Go's byte-identical scope_hash - verified 3d617ad3f63a5debe25c63c25475ccb63ee7494c8ac834c68bcd1cc09a736d65 for --robot-plan --label cli); and the unscoped baseline itself (46 issues, identical data_hash, identical scope_hash), so the loader and data-hash are not a source of the scoping diffs.

6. FIX ORDERING / DEPENDENCIES. --db and --workspace should land first (low-risk, high-confidence, and they fix source provenance for everything downstream). --repo next (self-contained, needs only filter_by_repo plus an existing hash helper). -l/-r plumbing next. --label needs the central scoping refactor and touches the triage output shape. --brief is independent and can go any time after -l lands. --recipe is last - it is a ~2000-line port of an entire engine, not a flag fix, and it is the only entry here that should not be attempted as a patch.

AUDIT HYGIENE: I edited no files in either repo. All fixtures were created under /tmp (outside both repos): /tmp/bvdb/.beads (3-issue store), /tmp/bvws/.bv/workspace.yaml, /tmp/bvws2 (nested .beads under a parent workspace). cargo build -p bv was a no-op ("Finished in 0.56s"), confirming target/debug/bvr.exe matches HEAD 36d05d0.
verifierSummary:
I tried to refute all 8 entries and could not refute any of them. Every gap re-reproduced with my own diff_robot.sh runs (I also rebuilt bv into an out-of-repo CARGO_TARGET_DIR to be sure the binary matched HEAD; results were identical to the in-repo one). No documented scope cut in AGENTS.md or COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md covers these flags - the plan explicitly lists recipes and workspace under "Core parity (must ship in v1)" (line 141) and records scope cuts for search, causality, network, sprints, correlator and attention scoring, none of which touch scoping. All eight are reachable from the CLI (I ran each), and none is TUI-only.

However, the audit has three material errors and several gaps that would leave the implementer short of byte-parity:

1. MISSED DEFECT affecting --label, --recipe and --repo equally: the envelope's `scope` object is emitted in the WRONG POSITION. Go's RobotEnvelope (cmd/bv/main.go:7215-7230) declares Scope after SourceKind, i.e. between source_kind and source_authority; Rust inserts it after scope_hash (crates/bv/src/main.rs:2623-2644). Verified via Object.keys on both binaries for --robot-plan/--robot-priority/--robot-insights --label cli. The audit called envelope reporting "correct" and "verified byte-identical" - only the scope_hash VALUE matches, not the serialization. No scoped invocation can reach byte-identity until this is fixed.

2. MISSED SCOPE: Go emits top-level `label_scope` + `label_context` on --robot-insights as well as --robot-plan and --robot-priority; the audit's implementation step (d) names only plan and priority.

3. MISSED SUB-GAP in --workspace, which makes its implementation advice insufficient: even when Rust's workspace loader IS reached it does not match Go. Same config -> Go data_hash bc6f99e80eea7432..., Rust a16daa9eacd03130.... Go's namespaceIssues (pkg/workspace/loader.go:563-600) rewrites dep.IssueID, dep.DependsOnID and comment.IssueID; the Rust loader (crates/bv-core/src/workspace.rs:244-252) rewrites only dep.depends_on_id, and compute_issue_dependency_hash hashes dep.issue_id (crates/bv-core/src/data_hash.rs:224), which the JSONL populates. Rust also sets source_repo = repo name where Go uses sourceRepoKeyFromPrefix(prefix).

4. WRONG FIX LOCATION for --db path normalization: Go normalizes inside resolveBeadsRedirect via filepath.Abs (pkg/loader/loader.go:266-268), which covers BEADS_DB, BEADS_DIR and the default .beads path. Rust's follow_beads_redirect (crates/bv-core/src/discovery.rs:99-127) has no equivalent. The audit put the / -> \ conversion in a new apply_db_flag helper; that fixes --db but leaves the mixed-separator bug for BEADS_DB/BEADS_DIR users - the very bug the audit itself surfaced.

5. Two evidence-quality problems. The -l and -r "byte-size proof" is unsound: Rust's payload contains float `.status.*.ms` timing fields, so sizes drift between identical runs (I measured 8854 / 8867 / 8854 for three runs the audit reported as 8880 / 8854 / 8854). The sound proof - which I ran - is that a leaf diff of `bvr --robot-triage` vs `bvr --robot-triage -l cli` differs in EXACTLY two leaves, both `.ms` floats. And the -l blastRadius line "also fixes -f as well" is wrong: output_format() reads an atomic set from the already-rewritten args, and `-f toon` is ignored identically by Go and Rust (go=16356B / rust=8854B, both JSON). There are six raw env::args() readers, not four (main.rs:21 correct, 574, 655, 2205, 5146, 6712).

What I independently confirmed as stated: filterByRepo semantics including the trailing-':' case; compute_data_hash returning "empty"; Go's candidate-set gating in pkg/analysis/triage.go:610-616/638-641 and IsCandidate at graph.go:1358; scopeLoadedIssues at main.go:4870-4933 and discoverWorkspaceConfig at main.go:9969-9981; the recipe resolution site at main.go:2581-2606; the --brief encoder at robot_registry.go:2292-2323 and its single consumption site at :2232; and that --robot-recipes and unscoped --robot-orphans are already byte-identical (so --robot-recipes is a safe thing to re-source from a new loader).

Fix ordering the audit proposed is sound: --db and --workspace (source provenance, plus the workspace loader's dep.issue_id/comment qualification and the source_meta_for threading) first, then --repo, then the argv-reader fix for -l/-r, then --label's central-scoping refactor, --brief independently, --recipe last. I edited nothing in either repo; fixtures live under /tmp (bvdbA, bvwsA, bvwsB) and the alternate build under /tmp/bvr_audit_target.

flags.goBehavior: Global scoping modifier applied by scopeLoadedIssues (cmd/bv/main.go:4870-4933) which runs ONCE before the whole robot dispatch, so every --robot-* handler inherits the narrowed RobotContext. Order inside the function is: (1) --repo filter, (2) --label subgraph, (3) --recipe. For --label specifically: ComputeLabelSubgraph (pkg/analysis/label_health.go:1351) builds CoreIssues (issues whose Labels contains the label, exact match) + DependencyIssues (each core issue's blockers it DependsOn, plus every issue that declares a dependency on a core issue - untyped, both directions). ctx.CandidateIDs = CoreIssues; ctx.Issues = AllIssues (core + neighbours). DataHash is NOT recomputed (the loader hash survives) and DataHashMatchesIssues is set false. It also builds ctx.LabelContext = the label's entry in ComputeAllLabelHealth over the final set. The Analyzer is constructed with SetReadinessScope(readiness, CandidateIDs) (cmd/bv/robot_registry.go:225-230) and IsCandidate (pkg/analysis/graph.go:1358) gates counts and recommendations: ComputeTriageFromAnalyzer builds candidateIssues = issues.filter(analyzer.IsCandidate) and runs computeCountsWithContext over THAT (pkg/analysis/triage.go:610-616), and filters allRecommendations by IsCandidate (triage.go:638-641). Envelope emits scope.label and scope_hash = robotScopeHash(label, recipe, repo, dataHash, sorted candidate ids) (robot_registry.go:257-268); robot-plan/robot-priority additionally emit top-level label_scope + label_context.
flags.rustBehavior: Envelope-level reporting is correct: active_scope_flags() reads --label and full_envelope_json_with_source (main.rs:2617-2643) emits scope.label and computes scope_hash from label_scope_ids() - verified byte-identical scope_hash vs Go for --robot-plan --label cli (3d617ad3f63a5debe25c63c25475ccb63ee7494c8ac834c68bcd1cc09a736d65). The ANALYSIS SET, however, is only narrowed in two of the robot commands. apply_label_scope (main.rs:686-699) is called at exactly two sites: run_robot_triage (main.rs:1111) and run_robot_alerts (main.rs:5178). run_robot_insights, run_robot_plan, run_robot_priority, run_robot_orphans and every other handler call load_issues_auto_meta and never call it, so they analyse all 46 issues while claiming scope.label in the envelope. flags.goBehavior:
Three distinct behaviours.
(1) The explicit flag: `workspaceConfig := flag.String("workspace", ...)` (main.go:1539). With it set and --as-of empty, the load block at main.go:2678-2721 calls workspace.LoadAllFromConfig(ctx, *workspaceConfig), which resolves the workspace root as filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(configPath)) (pkg/workspace/loader.go:628), loads every enabled repo, and builds a multi-source RobotSourceAuthority. source_kind becomes "workspace" and source_path the config path (main.go:2805-2807).
(2) Auto-discovery, main.go:2624-2631, guarded by discoverWorkspaceConfig (main.go:9969-9981): it first calls loader.GetBeadsDir(""); if that succeeds AND the returned path exists as a directory it returns "" immediately. Only when there is NO reachable .beads directory does it walk up looking for .bv/workspace.yaml. So a local .beads always wins over an ancestor workspace.yaml. Auto-discovery is also disabled when --as-of is set, and then main.go:2636-2638 prints "Warning: --workspace is ignored when --as-of is specified".
(3) Scope interaction: a workspace load leaves CandidateIDs nil, so --label and --repo still narrow it afterwards; source_tombstoneIDs are accumulated from every successful repo (main.go:2697-2701).
flags.rustBehavior:
The flag is never read - nothing in the tree matches "--workspace". load_issues_auto_meta (main.rs:769) only calls bv_core::workspace::find_workspace_config(cwd), which walks UP from cwd; an explicit --workspace path is invisible. Two further defects on the auto-discovery path:
(A) The order is inverted. find_workspace_config is consulted UNCONDITIONALLY and FIRST, before get_beads_dir. Go does the opposite - .beads wins. So in a project that has both its own .beads/ and an ancestor .bv/workspace.yaml, Rust silently loads the workspace while Go loads the project.
(B) When that happens the reported provenance is wrong. run_robot_triage computes the envelope source via source_meta_for(&loaded) (main.rs:1130), which re-derives path/kind from get_beads_dir(cwd) + find_jsonl_path, ignoring the fact that the issues actually came from the workspace. auditNotes:
CROSS-CUTTING (affects every flag in this group and the whole CLI): a zero-length argv element panics the Rust binary. `crates/bv/src/argv.rs:38` computes `arg[1..].find('=').unwrap_or(arg.len() - 1)` BEFORE the `arg.len() > 2` guard on line 39, so `--anything ""` panics with `start byte index 1 is out of bounds for string of length 0` and exits 101. Go handles every one of these. Confirmed for all seven of my flags: `--history-since ''` go=0/rust=101, `--min-confidence ''` go=1/rust=101, `--history-limit ''` go=1/rust=101, `--robot-history-timeout-ms ''` go=1/rust=101, `--robot-not-ready-labels ''` go=0/rust=101, `--bead-history ''` go=0/rust=101, `--id-pattern ''` go=0/rust=101. Fix: length-check before slicing.

SHARED ERROR-TEXT GAP: the modifier-requires failure's first line matches Go byte-for-byte in all my tests, but the second line does not. Go appends `\nTry: \`{example}\`.` from `modifierRecoveryExamples` (main.go:257-317) via `formatModifierRecoveryExamples` (main.go:237-255), and prints NOTHING when the modifier has no example. Rust unconditionally prints `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)` (crates/bv/src/main.rs:49). Affects --history-since, --history-limit and --min-confidence (all three share Go's history-since example, per the `case "history-since", "history-limit", "min-confidence"` arm at main.go:279-280) and --robot-history-timeout-ms (`bv robot-triage --robot-history-timeout-ms 10000 --json`, main.go:281-282). `ValidationError::MissingRequirement` (crates/bv/src/validation.rs:11-16) already carries `modifier`, so a per-flag example table keyed on it is a small, local change. This is a single shared fix — do it once, not once per flag.

BASELINE NOISE, NOT A PORT BUG: every `--robot-history` diff shows `.stats.strategies[0..2].duration_ms` differing, and nothing else. Both sides measure real wall time (`Go pkg/correlation/correlator.go:249,272,288 via durationMS at 294-296; Rust crates/bv-correlation/src/history.rs:1377,1408,1424,1436`) and both DISK-CACHE the result keyed on (HEAD, beads, opts) — Go at pkg/correlation/disk_cache.go:390-420. That is why Go's numbers are identical across repeated runs (233.737, 1.387, 0 three times in a row) yet differ from Rust's. No implementation change can make these match. Judge `--robot-history` flags by "are duration_ms the ONLY leaves in the diff", not by byte-identical.

CACHE GOTCHA FOR SIBLINGS: the correlation disk cache keys on CorrelatorOptions but NOT on process-global state. `--id-pattern` is invisible while the cache is warm. Export `BV_NO_CACHE=1` (Go pkg/correlation/disk_cache.go:97-102; both binaries honour it) before auditing any flag that feeds the correlator, or you will get a false "parity".

PRE-EXISTING GAPS THAT BLOCK ISOLATION (belong to other groups, not mine): `--robot-next` and `--robot-triage` are ALREADY divergent in Rust before any of my flags are applied — Rust omits `.actions.claim`, `.actions.show`, `.claim_command`, `.actionable`, `.id` and the whole recommendation-actions block (go=5310B vs rust=2346B for --robot-next; go=16356B vs rust=8854B for --robot-triage). This is a live-action/claim-routing gap. Anyone auditing --robot-not-ready-labels or --robot-history-timeout-ms through those two commands will see this noise first and may mis-attribute it; I worked around it by testing through the bare `--robot-not-ready-labels` invocation, which routes to the triage payload in both binaries.

UNSOLVED / NOT ESTABLISHED: I did not test `--id-pattern` interaction with `--robot-orphans` on a real bh--style repo (this repo has none), so the orphan-side wiring beyond the existing stub call site is unverified. I also did not audit `--history-limit`/`--history-since` against `--robot-orphans` and `--robot-causality` beyond the one byte-identical causality run. Go's integer-overflow rejection was tested for --robot-history-timeout-ms but NOT for --history-limit. The Rust triage limit 200-vs-500 rule (Go robot_registry.go:2171-2177) I judged unreachable but did not prove.
verifierSummary:
All seven gap claims survived re-derivation — I reproduced every behavioural divergence with my own diff_robot.sh runs — so the previous report is not over-claiming gaps. Two entries carry materially wrong implementation advice, and one missed a reachable gap, so I refute those two.

Refuted (gap real, advice wrong):
- --bead-history: the named code locations are wrong. `bead-history` is at flags.rs:1599 in MODIFIER_FLAGS and is ALREADY primary:false; flags.rs:1858-1859 is the help-category array `const HISTORY`, not a primary table. `ROBOT_PRIMARY_NAMES` (argv.rs:228) already mirrors Go's `primaryRobotFlagNames` and already omits bead-history, so "add a primary_robot_flag_names() helper" is redundant. The real root cause is `validate_exclusive_primaries` (validation.rs:84) iterating only `primary: true` ROBOT_PRIMARIES, so the {robot-history, bead-history} group is never populated. Two MISSED gaps: the `history <id>` subcommand alias (Go's rewriteRobotValueIntent forwards the value to --bead-history; Rust's ALIASES drops it — reproduced 8044B vs 267470B), and case-insensitive `--output JSON` detection (go=1 vs rust=0).
- --min-confidence: the gap is real and is the worst of the group (silent unfiltered output where Go refuses). But the fix rests on a non-existent argv type-validation layer: `FlagKind` is read only at main.rs:6950-6952 for help rendering, and the help text is ALREADY byte-identical. Following the advice literally converts a silent-wrong-output bug into a wrong-error-text bug.

Also corrected (verdict stands, mechanism corrected): --history-since blank handling is already correct and cannot fix the `""` case (the panic is in argv.rs:38, before dispatch); --history-limit and --robot-history-timeout-ms share the same false argv-layer premise; the report's claim that Go's 500->200 triage limit rule is "unreachable" is wrong — `--history-limit` requires a history primary, so `cfg.HistoryLimit` is always nil on the triage path and the coercion always fires.

Unchanged and confirmed: --history-limit (abc go=1/rust=2, " 5 " go=1/rust=0, value plumbing correct), --id-pattern (candidates 162 vs 24 with BV_NO_CACHE=1, invalid regex go=2 vs rust=0, warm-cache masking confirmed on both sides), --robot-history-timeout-ms (unpinned 1ms -> go "timeout" vs rust "ok"; correctly a no-op on both sides under the pinned clock), --robot-not-ready-labels (Go drops 2 top_picks and flips 2 claimable to false, case-insensitively; Rust unchanged — though the previous report's size-based evidence for this was confounded by the pre-existing --robot-triage claim gap and had to be re-derived with a Go-vs-Go baseline).

Cross-cutting, both confirmed: the argv.rs:38 empty-argument panic (go=0/1 vs rust=101 for all seven flags) and the modifier-requires recovery line (Go appends `Try: `bv robot-history --history-since "30 days ago" --json`.` or prints nothing when the modifier has no example; Rust unconditionally prints a `Usage: bvr --robot-help` line). Also surfaced one out-of-group drift the implementer will hit in the same helper: ROBOT_PRIMARY_NAMES has a spurious `robot-alerts` entry, so `--robot-alerts --json` gives go=1 vs rust=0.

Nothing in this group is a documented scope cut. AGENTS.md and COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN 4.5/4.6 list --id-pattern's process-global registry and the BV_ROBOT_HISTORY_TIMEOUT_MS deadline threading as REQUIRED work, and the plan's "confirmed remaining gaps" section calls --robot-not-ready-labels' claimability wiring out as not-yet-done (which agrees with the audit).

But main.rs:219 routes on `presence.has("robot-history") || presence.has("bead-history")`, so Rust treats `--bead-history` as a primary and never errors. `flags.rs:1858-1859` lists both as primaries, and `ROBOT_PRIMARIES` therefore has no `{"robot-history","bead-history"}`-style modifier-only grouping nor the `hasPrimaryRobotArg` name set that drives Go's default-`--robot-triage` injection.

flags.verifierReason: Gap is REAL (reproduced), but the code-level diagnosis is factually wrong on two of its three named locations, and the audit missed two reachable sub-gaps. (1) FALSE: 'flags.rs:1858-1859 lists both as primaries'. flags.rs:1858-1859 is the `const HISTORY: &[&str]` help-CATEGORY array inside the help renderer, not a primary table. `bead-history` is declared at flags.rs:1599 inside `MODIFIER_FLAGS` and is ALREADY `primary: false`. The advice 'Give bead-history the same primary: false treatment the other modifiers get' is therefore a no-op. (2) FALSE/redundant: 'add a primary_robot_flag_names() helper mirroring Go main.go:1096-1134' — it already exists as `ROBOT_PRIMARY_NAMES` (argv.rs:228) and already correctly omits bead-history; I diffed the two lists and they are identical except Rust has one extra `robot-alerts`. (3) The REAL root cause, which the report only mentions in passing, is that `validate_exclusive_primaries` (validation.rs:84-100) iterates only `ROBOT_PRIMARIES` entries with `primary: true`, so `bead-history` is never counted in the `group: Some("history")` bucket; Go counts it via `primaryRobotCommandGroups` = {flags:["robot-history","bead-history"]} (main.go:1870) with `isFlagActive` non-blank-string semantics. (4) MISSED GAP: the `history <bead-id>` subcommand alias. Go's `rewriteRobotValueIntent` (main.go:613, 728, 822-840) rewrites `history X` -> `--robot-history --bead-history X`; Rust's ALIASES table (argv.rs:60) maps `history` -> `--robot-history` only and drops the value. Reproduced: `diff_robot.sh history beads_viewer_rust-api-freeze-b73 --json` -> go=8044B bead-filtered, rust=267470B unfiltered. The previous report listed this exact command in its testPlan but never ran it. (5) MISSED GAP: `contains_structured_output_alias` (argv.rs:209-217) compares `--output <fmt>` case-sensitively while Go's `isRobotOutputFormat` (main.go:1145-1153) lowercases and trims. Reproduced: `--bead-history=<id> --output JSON` -> go=1, rust=0.

flags.goBehavior: main.go:1547. `handleRobotHistory` (robot_registry.go:2606-2614) only parses when the value is non-blank, calls `recipe.ParseRelativeTime(*cfg.HistorySince, robotNow())`, and a parse error is fatal: `fmt.Errorf("parsing --history-since: %w", err)`. `ParseRelativeTime` (pkg/recipe/types.go:263-304) trims, tries `^(\d+)([dwmy])$` case-insensitively via `now.AddDate(...)`, then RFC3339 / `2006-01-02T15:04:05` / `2006-01-02` with `ParseInLocation`. A blank value short-circuits to the zero time with no error (types.go:264-266). The dispatch wrapper prefixes the message: `Error handling --robot-history: ` and `TimeParseError` renders `invalid time format: X (expected relative like '14d', '2w', '1m' or ISO date)`. Also read by `--robot-causality` at robot_registry.go:3464.
flags.rustBehavior: crates/bv/src/main.rs:2321-2330 calls `parse_relative_time(&since)` (main.rs:2270-2286) and on `Err` prints `Error: parsing --history-since: {e}` where `e` is `could not parse time "{raw}"`, exit 1. The value is correctly threaded into `opts.since` on success, and `--robot-causality` parity is confirmed byte-identical.

flags.verifierReason: Gap is REAL and I reproduced all three facets. (a) ZERO UNITS: `--robot-history --history-since 0d --json` -> go=0 with a 222534B report (distinct from the 267461B unfiltered baseline, so Go really does apply Since=now), rust=1 `Error: parsing --history-since: could not parse time "0d"`. Same for 0w. auditNotes:
Structural findings that a sibling auditor should know (all verified with direct runs + diff_robot.sh, none caused by the flags in this group):

1. RUST'S TOON EMITTER DOES NOT EXIST. crates/bv/src/main.rs:2648 `emit_json` is the sole terminal emitter and prints JSON unconditionally. crates/bv-robot/src/envelope.rs:239-341 only *probes* for `tru` (is_toonRustBinary) so main.rs:193 can decide the downgrade warning — nothing ever calls `tru --encode`. With a working `tru` on PATH, Rust emits raw JSON while `"output_format":"toon"` claims TOON. I proved this with a stub tru.exe in %TEMP%\trustub (built with rustc, outside both repos, selected via the TOON_TRU_BIN env var that both the Go vendor toon-go and the Rust port honour). This is the hard blocker for `--stats` and it will affect whatever auditor owns `--format` / `--toon` / BV_OUTPUT_FORMAT / TOON_DEFAULT_FORMAT / TOON_KEY_FOLDING / TOON_INDENT. Recommend coordinating so the encoder lands once.

2. `--format=toon` (EQUALS FORM) IS SILENTLY IGNORED BY RUST. main.rs:178-183 does `args.iter().position(|a| a == "--format")`, which cannot match the token `--format=toon`; `fmt_val` falls back to "json". Observed: `TOON_TRU_BIN=<stub> ./target/debug/bvr.exe --robot-next --format=toon --stats` produced NO `warning: tru not available` on stderr while the Go oracle produced it. The space form `--format toon` behaves correctly. This is a --format bug but it silently corrupts any test that uses the equals form.

3. RUST CALLS std::env::set_var ZERO TIMES in crates/bv/src/main.rs. Go sets BV_ROBOT=1 (main.go:2021-2027), BEADS_DB from --db (main.go:1933-1941) and BV_NO_CACHE from --no-cache (main.go:1946-1949) at startup. Rust sets none of them, so every env-gated subsystem downstream (the analysis disk cache at cache.rs:69, the correlation disk cache, parsers keyed off BV_ROBOT) is inert regardless of the CLI flag. Whoever wires the disk cache should land the set_var block first.

4. PRE-EXISTING BASELINE DIFF, NOT ANY OF MY FLAGS: `.status.<Metric>.ms` is emitted by Rust on --robot-insights, --robot-priority and --robot-plan but NOT by Go. 9 leaves, e.g. `.status.Betweenness.ms = 0.3144`, `.status.PageRank.ms = 0.26739...`. Present in every flag-off baseline I measured. Given diff_robot.sh pins SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, wall-clock `ms` values would never be byte-stable anyway, so this is probably meant to be suppressed or rounded when the clock is pinned. Flag it to whoever owns the `status` sub-object.

5. RUST'S ROBOT-TRIAGE OUTPUT IS UNSTABLE RUN-TO-RUN. Successive identical `./scripts/diff_robot.sh --robot-triage` invocations produced rust=8853B / 8854B / 8867B with no flag change. The 13-byte jitter is NOT caused by --no-cache (I chased it and it reproduces on the bare baseline). Anyone diffing a payload whose size they are using as evidence should re-run twice and compare leaf sets, not byte counts.

6. VALIDATION EMITTER DIVERGES GLOBALLY. crates/bv/src/main.rs:50 unconditionally appends `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)` after every modifier-requires violation. Go's flag package prints only `Error: --profile-json requires --profile-startup` and exits 1. This affects every rule in flags.rs MODIFIER_REQUIRES (~40 rules), not just my group. Fixing it removes the one remaining delta on `--profile-json`.

7. Rust's `crates/bv-analysis/src/cache.rs` `AnalysisCache` is DEAD CODE outside its own tests — `disk_cache_enabled()` (cache.rs:67) and the whole LRU have zero production callers. I verified by `BV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/bvcache`: Go --robot-priority writes analysis_cache/<sha>.json + .lock, Rust writes 0 files in any mode. The Go cache is output-neutral (cold run vs warm run stdout byte-identical via `cmp`), so porting it is a performance-only change — but it must ship together with finding #3 or it will never arm.

8. FLAG-KIND TABLE CONTRADICTS ARGV PARSER. crates/bv/src/flags.rs declares the authoritative types (`s("cpu-profile")` at 1561, `b(...)` for the rest) but crates/bv/src/argv.rs:309-323 re-derives the same set by hand for `flag_takes_value` and got `cpu-profile` wrong. Consider having argv.rs read flags.rs's table instead of duplicating it — that removes the whole class of bug.
verifierSummary: All six gap verdicts survive re-derivation — I reproduced every one with my own diff_robot.sh runs and direct invocations — but the previous agent's implementation advice is materially wrong on five of six, so I refute those entries rather than let the implementer act on it. Confirmed gaps: --force-full-analysis (22 GO-only leaves on --robot-plan, 5 on --robot-priority; field values in the advice are exactly right), --stats (independently re-proved with my own stub tru: Go prints `[stats] JSON≈1328 tok, TOON≈5 tok (TOON 99% smaller)`, Rust prints nothing and emits raw JSON), --profile-startup (Go exit 0 / 652B report, Rust exit 124 TUI hang), --cpu-profile (Go writes the .prof and exits 1 with `Could not create CPU profile:` on a bad path; Rust is silent at exit 0, and argv.rs:321 mis-types the flag as boolean). --profile-json is correctly "partial". Corrections that matter: (1) `--no-cache` is not-applicable, not a gap — `env.NoCache` has exactly two readers in the entire Go tree, both disk-cache gates, and Rust ships neither an analysis cache nor a correlation cache (crates/bv-correlation/src/correlator.rs:11 says so in its own module doc), so the flag's meaning is already vacuously satisfied and every observable contract matches. (2) The advice to "delete the Usage: line because Go's flag package prints no usage line" is flatly false — Go emits a per-modifier `Try:` hint (main.go:238-310), proven with `--graph-depth 3` and `--severity warning`; and Go returns on the FIRST modifier violation while Rust prints all, proven with `--graph-depth 3 --severity warning`. (3) `--profile-startup` must be placed upstream of Rust's check-drift/save-baseline (main.rs:206/212), not after robot-alerts as advised — I measured `--check-drift --profile-startup`: Go prints the profile (exit 0), Rust prints "No baseline found" (exit 1). (4) `--force-full-analysis` is consumed by --save-baseline (Go main.go:3575) and --check-drift (main.go:3654) too — both implemented in Rust — contradicting the advice's "no other command consumes the flag in Go either". (5) The --stats TOON advice would pass `--delimiter`/`--indent` that Go omits at defaults (vendor toon-go/toon.go:217-229), and names the private `tru_path()`. (6) The --cpu-profile test plan asserts `--help` leaves a profile file; Go writes none (flag.Parse exits before main.go:1910). Also: Rust's `encode_payload` comment claiming "Go's TOON is byte-identical to compact JSON" is false — golden/toon/selfrepo__robot_next.toon literally contains `"output_format":"json"`, i.e. the goldens were captured on a box with no `tru`, so the corpus is not evidence of TOON parity.

auditNotes:
Method. I used --robot-recipes as the carrier for every headless diff because it is one of only two commands in this repo that are currently byte-identical (the other is --robot-schema), so any diff is attributable to the flag under test. --robot-triage is NOT a clean baseline: it has a pre-existing 95-leaf diff (missing .triage.commands.claim_top/show_top and .recommendations[*].actions.{claim,show}) unrelated to this group. Do not use it as a control. --robot-capabilities (409 leaves), --robot-sprint-list (Rust emits an extra .issue_count) and --robot-capacity (14 missing .actionable entries) also have pre-existing diffs.

Four cross-cutting structural facts a sibling auditor should know:

1. THE BIGGEST BUG IN THIS GROUP IS AN OFF-BY-ONE, NOT A FLAG. crates/bv/src/argv.rs:138 reads `if out.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()) == Some("--update")`, but rewrite_args receives argv WITHOUT the program name: crates/bv/src/main.rs:21-22 does `let raw: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect(); let args = argv::rewrite_args(&raw);`, and the alias loop at argv.rs:120-131 scans from index 0. So the entire rewriteUpgradeIntent port (argv.rs:138-174) is DEAD CODE in the real binary. Its unit test upgrade_subcommand_variants (argv.rs:521-539) passes only because the test helper prepends a synthetic "bvr". Observable impact: `bv upgrade check` runs --update instead of --check-update (wrong message: "is already up to date" vs "is up to date"); `bv upgrade rollback` runs --update and exits 0 where Go attempts a rollback and exits 1; `bv upgrade dry-run` runs --update. The fix is index 1 -> index 0, plus updating the test helper so it stops passing a program name, otherwise the test starts failing and hides regressions. NOTE: this bug is live TODAY, so any flag-audit run that exercised `bv upgrade <mode>` may have mis-attributed it.

2. RUST HAS NO FLAG-ARITY VALIDATION AT ALL. crates/bv/src/validation.rs:34-42 (Presence::from_args) strips -- from every token and inserts it into a HashSet, with no notion of a flag consuming the next token. Go relies on pflag, so a bare --debug-render, --theme, --debug-width or --debug-height is a parse error (exit 1, `flag needs an argument: --X` / `Use --X VALUE. ...` via cmd/bv/main.go:1267-1271), while Rust accepts it and proceeds (and standalone, launches the TUI). Verified for all four. Worse, Rust also treats flag VALUES as flag names, so a value colliding with a flag name can produce phantom validation violations. This one fix covers every string/int flag in the inventory.

3. RUST HAS NO modifierRecoveryExamples PORT. Go's cmd/bv/main.go:257-316 maps ~20 modifiers to recovery examples, formatted by main.go:238-255 (`Try:` for one, `Try one of:` for several). Rust prints a single hardcoded `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)` (crates/bv/src/main.rs:46-51) for EVERY validation violation, including exclusive-primary ones which Go does not decorate at all. Any sibling auditing modifier-requires flags (--search-limit, --attention-limit, --schema-command, --suggest-type, --severity, --history-since, --graph-*, ...) will find the same stderr diff and the same single fix.

4. THE PRODUCT NAME IS INCONSISTENT WITHIN RUST. crates/bv/src/flags.rs:60 already sets HELP_PROGRAM = "bv" with an explicit byte-parity rationale, and crates/bv/src/main.rs:1558 already defines GO_APP_VERSION = "v0.25.0" and uses it for robot-docs, robot-capabilities and the env payload. But --version (main.rs:35) and the entire update family (main.rs:1619, 1631, 1648, 1654, 1676, 1691, 1718) hardcode "bvr" and read CARGO_PKG_VERSION. Whoever fixes this should introduce ONE program-name constant and ONE version constant and route all Go-visible strings through them, rather than patching 8 string literals individually.

Two smaller shared defects found while auditing the update flags: (a) crates/bv-update/src/github.rs:50 formats the GitHub error as `github api returned status {0}` with a bare u16 (populated at github.rs:115 and :143 via resp.status().as_u16()), while Go's cmd at pkg/updater/updater.go:344 and :634 uses resp.Status, which is "403 Forbidden" (observed live under rate limiting). (b) crates/bv-update/src/update.rs:67-71 calls std::fs::canonicalize(), which yields a \\?\ verbatim path on Windows, where Go's filepath.EvalSymlinks (pkg/updater/updater.go:1247) does not; this shows up verbatim in `Rollback failed: no backup found at \\?\C:\...`.

Genuinely out of scope for a headless drop-in: --background-mode and --no-background-mode (Go's only consumer is inside the TUI branch at cmd/bv/main.go:4492-4508, provably unreachable from any robot command; verified byte-identical). --debug-render's render body is borderline: it is NOT TTY-gated (Go prints a deterministic view string to stdout and exits 0) so it is technically headless, but matching it byte-for-byte requires the whole TUI model. Recommend splitting the fix: land the arity error and the `Unknown view:` arm now, treat the three real views as a separate TUI project.

Sandbox hazards for whoever runs this next: NEVER invoke these five flags bare (--yes, bare --rollback, --update without </dev/null, --debug-render, --generate-docs) - they either launch the interactive TUI and block, hit the network, or write files. Always pair with a robot carrier, redirect stdin from /dev/null, and wrap in `timeout 60`. The GitHub API rate-limits quickly from this IP; a 403 in a diff is usually transient, not a code difference. A batch of six update-flag runs hit it partway through and produced one misleading EXIT CODE MISMATCH that I re-ran to confirm was an artefact.

Could not verify: the `[dry-run] Would download ... for GOOS/GOARCH` line and the `Run 'bv upgrade' to apply.` trailer require a release newer than v0.25.0, which does not exist, so those two claims rest on source reading only. The --rollback SUCCESS path needs a <binary>.backup fixture, which I did not create (read-only rule); I suspect a duplicated "Rollback complete" in Rust (crates/bv-update/src/update.rs:535 and crates/bv/src/main.rs:1732 both print it) but did not confirm it. And --generate-docs writes docs/generated/*, README.md and AGENTS.md, so per the read-only rule I read Go's internal/docgen/docgen.go rather than running it; the only executed evidence for that flag is the stdout/exit-code difference.
verifierSummary:
I re-derived every entry from Go source plus fresh runs. All 13 verdicts survive: 10 gap, 2 not-applicable, 1 partial. Nothing is at parity, nothing is unreachable, and none is a documented scope cut (I read AGENTS.md and COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md: §2.2 lists the updater self-update flow as "Extended ... never blocks", but Rust already implements all four update handlers, so the surviving defects are string/routing bugs in already-shipped code, not a deferred feature; debug-render is scheduled as future TUI-M5 work at lines 416-417/334, again a "not yet done", not a cut). I set refuted=false throughout because the gaps themselves are real and demonstrated; instead I supply correctedImplementation for the six entries whose advice is wrong or incomplete. The material corrections, in priority order:

1. The pflag-arity fix MUST run ABOVE the --help short-circuit (crates/bv/src/main.rs:29-32), not merely above --version. Cobra parses flags before it consults --help, so `go --help --theme` exits 1 with `flag needs an argument: --theme` and empty stdout. This is a live diff the previous audit did not report: Rust currently prints its 18927-byte help and exits 0.

2. The arity check must model pflag's value CONSUMPTION, not just presence. pflag eats the next token verbatim even when it looks like a flag: `go --debug-render --robot-recipes` prints `Unknown view: --robot-recipes`; `go --theme --robot-recipes` warns about the value and then launches the TUI. Int flags additionally need Go's exact `invalid argument "X" for "--Y" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "X": invalid syntax` / `value out of range` text.

3. The --theme advice is factually wrong about the bare form. `flag.CommandLine.Changed("theme")` is never reached for a bare `--theme`; pflag rejects it first. Only `--theme=` (equals form) produces the empty-string warning.

4. The argv.rs fix as written is a NO-OP. Changing `out.get(1)` to `out.get(0)` alone leaves `skip(2)` and `vec![out[0].clone()]` intact, so `bv upgrade check` would still run --update. Go gates rewriteUpgradeIntent on the RAW first positional being upgrade/self-update/selfupdate and returns a fresh slice built from `rest`; the port must do the same. The unit test at argv.rs:521-539 also passes only because its helper prepends a synthetic program name, so it must change in the same edit.

5. MISSED GAP, highest blast radius: --robot-help and --robot-capabilities are dispatched in Go at main.go:2052/2054, BEFORE all four update handlers (2057/2075/2108/2162). Rust checks the update flags first. Reproduced for all four: `go=0/22994B capabilities JSON` vs `rust=1/0B` or `rust=0/35B "bvr is up to date"`. This belongs in every update-flag entry's blastRadius, not just --check-update.

6. The --version advice would reintroduce a hardcoded version, contradicting a deliberate documented decision at COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md:714 ("--version now reads env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION) instead of a hardcoded string"). The gap is real, but the fix is to bump the workspace version to 0.25.0 and expose one `v`-prefixed shared constant, which satisfies the plan and byte-parity at once — and incidentally repairs the same `0.2.0`-vs-`v0.25.0` mismatch in --robot-capabilities and --robot-metrics (re-diff those after the Cargo.toml bump).

7. I resolved the item the audit left open: Rust's `403 | 429 => Ok(None)` in check_for_updates is NOT deliberate hardening. Go's checkForUpdates (pkg/updater/updater.go:342-345) has no such branch and propagates. The in-code "(Go parity)" comment is false. The plan's "403/429 silent" (line 315) describes intended Rust design, and AGENTS.md:87 says the Go code wins on conflict.

I also confirmed the audit's UNVERIFIED double-print: Go prints "Rollback complete" inside Rollback (updater.go:1560) and main.go adds nothing; Rust prints it in both update.rs:533 and main.rs:1732. Still not executable without a backup fixture, so it remains code-level.

Two process notes. First, the previous audit's evidence for --generate-docs came from `./scripts/diff_robot.sh --robot-recipes --generate-docs`, which runs Go's docgen with the Rust repo as cwd and WRITES to it — `docs/generated/` is untracked with today's timestamp as a result. I re-verified precedence in a scratch cwd outside both repos instead, and got an even stronger result: `go --generate-docs --version`, `--generate-docs --theme bogus` and `--generate-docs --robot-recipes` all exit 1 with empty stdout and a README-read error, proving docgen preempts everything while still writing its eight files first. Second, the GitHub API was rate-limited for most of my session, which made the update-flag error paths deterministic to compare; be aware that the exit-code asymmetry for `bv upgrade rollback` is network-state-dependent (403 -> both exit 1 with different messages; healthy -> Go exits 1, Rust exits 0). The previous audit reported "rust exits 0" for that case, which only holds on a healthy network.

Cross-cutting facts a sibling auditor should reuse: --robot-recipes is a clean byte-identical control; --robot-triage is not (pre-existing triage diffs). The hardcoded `Usage: bvr --robot-help ...` trailer at main.rs:46-51 is wrong for every validation violation — Go decorates only modifier-requires errors, via the ~60-line modifierRecoveryExamples switch at main.go:257-316, and decorates exclusive-primary errors with nothing at all (verified: `go --robot-triage --robot-next` prints one line, no trailer).

(1) In the pflag-arity layer (see --debug-render), treat --theme as a string flag: a bare `--theme` as the last token must produce the arity error and exit 1, NOT a theme warning.
