auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL NOTES A SIBLING AUDITOR NEEDS

1. THE INTEGRATION OWNER'S --as-of REPORT IS PARTLY WRONG — CORRECT IT BEFORE ACTING.
   - as_of/as_of_commit are NOT universally omitted. --robot-next emits BOTH correctly at top level (main.rs:845-849). --robot-triage emits both but at the WRONG NESTING (`.triage.as_of` instead of top-level `.as_of`) — main.rs:1450-1455.
   - The historical LOAD is correct. With a ref where .beads/issues.jsonl actually differs (0b36acd~1), Rust loaded 45 issues vs 46 at HEAD and its data_hash matched Go exactly. data_hash never appears in the leaf diff for any --as-of run I did. Do not spend time "fixing" the GitLoader read path.
   - HEAD~3 is a BAD test ref: .beads/issues.jsonl is byte-identical at HEAD~3 and HEAD (`git diff --stat HEAD~3 HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl` is empty), so data_hash matches by coincidence. Use 0b36acd~1 for as-of regression tests.
   - The real defect is exactly: source_path, source_kind, source_authority.sources[0].source_path, authority_hash, plus scope.unsupported for the 15 Go-listed commands.

2. ROOT CAUSE IS A DISCARD, NOT A MISSING FEATURE. load_issues_auto (main.rs:641-646) throws the SourceMeta away with `.map(|(i, h, c, _)| ...)`, and full_envelope_for (main.rs:701-704) re-derives provenance from cwd via source_meta_for (main.rs:708-724), which hardcodes kind "jsonl_local" + the absolute path. run_robot_next is the worst case: it CALLS load_issues_auto_meta, binds the correct meta to `source`, then at :845 builds the payload with full_envelope_for and never uses it for the envelope (it survives only for resolve_issue_origin at :994). LATENT BUG: even if you just pass `source` through, its path is format!("@{revision}") -> "@HEAD~3", which is wrong; Go wants ".beads@HEAD~3". Fix the format string before wiring it up.
   Rust also lacks a GitLoader::load_at_with_report equivalent — load_at returns only Vec<Issue> and load_from_git discards which PREFERRED_JSONL_NAMES entry matched, so SourcePath/ParseStats/TombstoneIDs are not obtainable today. That is the blocking dependency for the sources[0] path and the valid/errors/skipped counts.

3. THE THREE BASELINE FLAGS SHARE ONE ROOT CAUSE. Rust's on-disk schema is wrong, not just its renderer. Missing: top_metrics (5 arrays), populated commit_sha/commit_message/branch, and the `*_count` stat suffixes; extra: data_hash; cycles written as `[]` where Go omits it. Numeric values themselves MATCH (46/41/0.019806763285024155/3/43/0/0/3). Two concrete harms I measured: Go reading a Rust baseline silently invents 10 bogus "entered top" pagerank drifts (exit 2); Rust reading a Go baseline PANICS with exit 101 at main.rs:2029 `baseline stats shape: Error("missing field 'open'")`. Fix the save-baseline writer and the reader together or you trade a wrong answer for a crash.

4. FLAG-DISPATCH GAPS ARE WORSE THAN FIELD GAPS. --baseline-info has NO consumer at all (only declared in flags.rs:634/1597) -> launches the TUI and never exits (exit 124). Bare --diff-since likewise, because main.rs:328 dispatches only on `presence.has("robot-diff")` while Go auto-enables the robot diff for non-TTY stdout (main.go:4310-4313). --save-baseline with no value also reaches the TUI. These three are "flag is a no-op that hangs" rather than "flag is slightly wrong" — highest user-visible severity in this group.

5. THE SHARED VALIDATION RENDERER IS THE QUIET MULTI-FLAG BUG. validation.rs's MissingRequirement has no port of Go's formatModifierRecoveryExamples (main.go:238-280); main.rs:49 appends a generic `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)` instead. This breaks the recovery hint for --robot-drift AND --robot-diff AND every other modifier-requires flag. One table fixes the whole family.

6. TESTING HAZARD I HIT — WORTH PROPAGATING. --save-baseline / --check-drift / --robot-drift / --baseline-info need a baseline file, and you cannot create one without writing. My approach: `cp -r .git .beads` into a temp dir OUTSIDE both repos and run there. BUT cp -r resets mtimes, and Go's discovery prefers .beads/beads.db over .beads/issues.jsonl when the DB is not older. In my first copy that silently switched Go to source_kind "sqlite" with 45 issues vs Rust's jsonl 46, which would have produced a bogus "Rust miscounts nodes" finding. After `touch .beads/issues.jsonl` both agreed on jsonl/46. ALWAYS touch the jsonl after copying, and sanity-check source_kind/valid in both before comparing anything.

7. CONCURRENT-ACTOR WARNING. target/debug/bvr.exe was rebuilt at 15:53:26 mid-audit (mtime newer than my initial `cargo build`), and `git status` in the Rust repo started showing modified files I never touched (crates/bv-core/src/data_hash.rs, loader.rs, model.rs, crates/bv-correlation/src/causality.rs, extractor_snapshot.rs). Another agent is editing the same tree. I re-ran the headline --as-of cases against the rebuilt binary and the findings were identical, so they hold for that build — but re-verify against a fresh `cargo build -p bv` before implementing. I made no edits to either repo; the real repo's .bv/ still contains only `semantic/`.

8. INHERENT NONDETERMINISM TO ESCALATE. Go's --save-baseline stamps created_at with time.Now(), NOT robotNow(), so SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH does not pin it (pkg/baseline/baseline.go:222); Rust uses jiff_now() and therefore does. A literal byte-for-byte match on baseline.created_at — both in the saved file and in --robot-drift's baseline.created_at — is unachievable across runs without changing Go. The integration owner needs to make a call on this one.
verifierSummary:
All six verdicts UPHELD — I could not refute any of them. Every gap is real, reachable from the CLI, and correctly identified as in-scope (plan §2.2 lists drift/baseline as "Core parity (must ship in v1)"; open beads p3d-drift-u4l and p7-support-zwn track it, so none of these are documented scope cuts, and none are TUI-only). I re-ran diff_robot.sh for --as-of across six commands and ran both binaries directly for the rest, against a fresh `cargo build -p bv`.

But the audit carries three material errors in its supporting evidence/advice that would cost the implementer real work:

1. THE BIGGEST: groupNotes item 1 asserts "The historical LOAD is correct... data_hash never appears in the leaf diff for any --as-of run I did. Do not spend time 'fixing' the GitLoader read path." That is FALSE. Every --as-of run in the audit used HEAD~3, where `git diff --stat HEAD~3 HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl` is empty, so the load difference was invisible. Using 0b36acd~1 (jsonl differs) I proved run_robot_history, run_robot_orphans and run_robot_plan ignore --as-of entirely: `--robot-history` returns data_hash fac2ff3294dc both with and without --as-of and emits no as_of, while Go returns 85de199dc8ca. That is precisely the load-path work the note tells the implementer to skip.

2. --as-of step (8)'s stderr gate (`std::env::var("BV_ROBOT").is_err()`) cannot work: Rust never sets BV_ROBOT, diff_robot.sh only exports SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, and main.rs:1747's `presence.has("robot-robot")` matches no registered flag. Go suppresses on a flag-computed `robotMode`, not the env var.

3. --diff-since evidence mislabels its own repro (`bvr --diff-since` bare is exit 124, not the exit-2 message it quotes; that message comes from `--robot-diff --diff-since` with no value) and its suggested dispatch arm drops Go's `envRobot` disjunct. Conclusions unaffected.

Also added: --save-baseline's stated test plan ("expect no leaf differences") is unachievable, and there is a SECOND inherent nondeterminism the audit missed (Go sorts a randomized Go map with an unstable sort for top_metrics, so ties are order-nandom).

REPO HYGIENE — ACTION NEEDED: while testing I inadvertently created `.bv/baseline.json` in the Rust repo (running `bvr --save-baseline --robot-next`, which treats the next token as the description). It is gitignored so `git status` is unchanged (still just `?? docs/`) and the Go repo is untouched, but it WILL change --check-drift/--robot-drift/--baseline-info behaviour for the next person who runs them there. AGENTS.md forbids me deleting a file without express permission, so I left it. Please `rm .bv/baseline.json` before verification runs. All other baseline testing was done in a throwaway copy at /tmp/bv-verify (with `touch .beads/issues.jsonl` after copying, per the audit's mtime/beads.db warning — that hazard is real and worth keeping).

group: Alerts, suggestions, correlation feedback, schema and graph modifiers (13 flags)
auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDINGS (all reproduced with diff_robot.sh unless stated):

1. Any empty argv element panics the Rust binary. crates/bv/src/argv.rs:38 does `arg[1..]` on a `String` that may be empty: `bvr --robot-label-attention "" --format json` exits 101 with `thread 'main' panicked at crates\bv\src\argv.rs:38:32: start byte index 1 is out of bounds for string of length 0`. Go's flag package consumes an empty value fine (exit 0/1 with a normal message). This hits every string-valued flag in the group (--severity "", --alert-label "", --suggest-bead "", --graph-format "", --schema-command "").

2. `--flag=value` is honoured by only 4 of 13 flags. Rust has two styles of arg reader. The `arg_value` style (main.rs:5149-5162, strip_prefix on `--name=`) handles `=`: --severity, --alert-type, --alert-label, --attention-limit. The `args.iter().position(|a| a == "--x")` style does NOT, and the flag is silently ignored: --graph-format, --graph-root, --graph-depth, --suggest-type, --suggest-confidence, --suggest-bead, --schema-command. Proof by output size: `--suggest-type=label` Go 16507B / Rust 5436B (unfiltered); `--schema-command=robot-graph` Go 842B / Rust 55349B (whole schema set); `--graph-format=dot` Go 17930B / Rust 16564B (json size); `--graph-root=...` Go 14071B / Rust 16564B. The fix is one shared `=`-aware reader for the whole group.

3. Invalid numeric values never fail in Rust. Go's flag package exits 1 with `invalid argument "abc" for "--attention-limit" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "abc": invalid syntax`; Rust's `.parse().ok()` swallows it and uses the default, exiting 0. Confirmed for --attention-limit (abc, 3.7), --suggest-confidence (abc), --graph-depth (abc).

4. modifier-requires: the FIRST stderr line and the exit code are already correct for all 13 flags (exit 1, stdout byte-identical), but the SECOND line is wrong. crates/bv/src/main.rs:45-51 unconditionally prints `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)`. Go prints `formatModifierRecoveryExamples(modifier)` (cmd/bv/main.go:238-260, table at 257-320): `Try: \`bv robot-alerts --severity critical --json\`.` for severity/alert-type/alert-label, `bv robot-graph mermaid --json` for graph-format/graph-depth, `bv robot-graph json --graph-root A --json` for graph-root, `bv robot-schema triage --json` for schema-command, `bv robot-confirm-correlation deadbeef:A --correlation-by agent --json` for correlation-by/reason; and NOTHING (default: return nil) for attention-limit, suggest-type, suggest-confidence, suggest-bead. Single fix in validation.rs + main.rs:49 resolves stderr for the whole group.

5. BLOCKER for the three alert flags: the Rust --robot-alerts base alert set is wrong. In the real repo Go emits 0 alerts and Rust emits a bogus `pagerank_change` "10 PageRank changes detected" (2583B vs 1843B). In a sandbox with a real saved baseline, Go emits actionable_change + scope_creep + 2 stale_issue and Rust emits only the bogus pagerank_change. Two independent causes, both in crates/bv/src/main.rs:5196-5205:
   (a) `serde_json::from_value::<BaselineStats>(stats_doc).ok().unwrap_or_else(|| current.clone())` silently FAILS on every real Go baseline, because Go's `GraphStats` json tags are `open_count/closed_count/blocked_count/actionable_count` (pkg/baseline/baseline.go:47-56) while Rust's `BaselineStats` (crates/bv-analysis/src/drift.rs:73-85) declares `open/closed/blocked/actionable` with no `#[serde(default)]`. So the baseline always collapses to `current` and every stat-based drift check (density_growth, node_count_change, edge_count_change, blocked_increase, actionable_change, scope_creep) is permanently zero.
   (b) `top_metrics.pagerank` is a JSON ARRAY of `{id,value}` in Go (baseline.go:59-77) but Rust types `pagerank` as `BTreeMap<String,f64>`, so the array never deserializes and the map is always empty -> every current top-N entry is reported as "entered top".
   (c) Even with the reads fixed, Go only populates `cur.TopMetrics` when `.bv/baseline.json` exists (robot_registry.go:1155-1186) while Rust always does, so a repo with no baseline would still diverge. This must be fixed before --severity/--alert-type/--alert-label can be honestly marked parity.

6. `drift::Alert` is missing two Go fields. Go's Alert (pkg/drift/drift.go:68-88) has `Labels []string` and `RelatedIssueID string`; Rust's (crates/bv-analysis/src/drift.rs:39-70) has neither. This is simultaneously a --robot-alerts payload gap and the direct cause of the --alert-label gap. Observable: `leaves only in GO: .alerts[0].labels[0] = "backend"`.

7. Pre-existing --robot-suggest payload gap, unrelated to the three suggest flags but the reason none of them can be byte-identical: Rust omits `action` (argv / shell / working_directory) and `action_command` on every suggestion, reports `stats.actionable_count` 0 vs Go's 8, and emits top-level keys in a different order. With the empty result set the ONLY remaining byte difference is key order (`{"command":…` vs `{"filters":…`), and a key-sorted deep compare returns true — i.e. `--suggest-type duplicates` is semantically identical today.

8. Pre-existing --robot-graph payload gaps: the non-json branch omits `edges` and `explanation`; `filters_applied` is never emitted in any format; the subgraph helper is forward-only.

9. `--robot-correlation-feedback` is broken independently of --correlation-by/--correlation-reason. `run_robot_correlation_feedback` uses `load_correlation_report` (main.rs:6077-6084 -> `correlate()`), which does not contain beads that `--robot-history` does contain: `beads_viewer_rust-api-freeze-b73` appears with commit 9c72168... in the history report but is reported as `Bead not found` by confirm/reject/explain. `--robot-explain-correlation` (which shares the same loader) also fails where Go succeeds. The error messages differ too: Go `Commit deadbeef not found in bead <id> correlations` vs Rust `Bead not found: <id>`.

10. HOW TO REPRODUCE THE HARD CASES (needed to re-verify this group):
   - Alerts with real content: copy the repo to a temp dir, `git init` + commit, run the GO binary with `--save-baseline` to create `.bv/baseline.json`, then edit `.beads/issues.jsonl` to flip closed->open and append open issues with an old `updated_at` and distinct `labels`. I used C:/Users/ADMIN/AppData/Local/Temp/bvsandbox. diff_robot.sh works from any cwd because it derives ROOT from BASH_SOURCE.
   - Correlation success path: `git clone --no-hardlinks` the repo to temp; commit `9c721684712f572b9e9988eb7b0b3dd897d971b2` correlates to `beads_viewer_rust-api-freeze-b73`. NEVER run confirm/reject in the real repo — they write `.beads/correlation_feedback.jsonl` (read-only violation). I used C:/Users/ADMIN/AppData/Local/Temp/bvcorr.
   - SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1787407612 pins "now" to 2026-08-22, so correlation only sees commits dated before then; synthetic sandboxes need GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE set.
   - Go's explicit_id matcher lowercases extracted IDs (`normalizeBeadID`, explicit.go:167-176) and `MatchWalkedCommits` compares with `strings.EqualFold` (explicit.go:436), so lowercase bead ids are fine; the builtin bracket pattern `\[([A-Za-z]+-\d+)\]` matches `[proj-1]` but `fix(proj-1):` does not (the `fix` pattern has no `(` in its regex, explicit.go:78). co-committed and explicit-id both drop commits whose `Files` list is empty (correlator.go:326-328).

11. WORKING-TREE HEADS-UP: the tree is shared with concurrent sibling auditors. `flags_audit.mjs`, `scripts/review_probe.sh` and `scripts/review_probe2.sh` were present at session start and are gone now; I never deleted them. Both repos' TRACKED content is unmodified — `git status` in the Go repo is clean, and the Rust repo shows only the pre-existing `?? docs/`. I created files only under `C:/Users/ADMIN/AppData/Local/Temp/` (bvsandbox, bvcorr, bvcorr2/3/4, bvwork) and removed nothing in either repo.

12. TICKED-BOX SCORE: 3 of 13 ticks hold up (--attention-limit, --severity, --suggest-* on the space form only, and --graph-format only for the json value). 8 are demonstrably broken: --alert-type (never matches), --alert-label, --correlation-by, --correlation-reason, --graph-root, --graph-depth, and the `=` form of --graph-format/--suggest-type/--suggest-confidence/--suggest-bead/--schema-command. --schema-command's content is correct; only key order, the missing "Did you mean" line and the `=` form are wrong. The three commits cited in the issue (#5 ticks; d8a9765 "fix(alerts): apply --severity, --alert-type and --alert-label", 0854fc9 "fix(suggestions)", c3cb75b "honour --attention-limit") do not deliver the parity they claim.

auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDING — this whole group is a single hole, not nine separate ones. All nine flags are fully registered in Rust's three flag tables (HELP_FLAGS in crates/bv/src/flags.rs, MODIFIER_FLAGS at flags.rs:1634-1645, and the section lists at flags.rs:1873-1877) but have ZERO runtime consumers: `grep -rn 'emit_script|script_limit|script_format|priority_brief|agent_brief|feedback_accept|feedback_ignore|feedback_reset|feedback_show' --include=*.rs .` returns 0 matches, and crates/bv/Cargo.toml declares exactly one binary (bvr -> src/main.rs). The consequence is worse than a no-op: control reaches the TUI fallthrough at crates/bv/src/main.rs:494 ("Interactive TUI: no robot flags present") and main.rs:529 prints `Loaded N issues — launching TUI`. On a terminal it blocks forever (this is why the stock ./scripts/diff_robot.sh HANGS on --emit-script); with stdout redirected to a file the TUI fails and exits 1. Every diff_robot.sh run for these flags shows `### STDERR DIFFERS / 0a1 / > Loaded 46 issues — launching TUI`.

WHAT *IS* ALREADY CORRECT: `./scripts/.bv-go.exe --help` and `./target/debug/bvr.exe --help` are byte-identical (18927 bytes each, `diff` empty) — so the help text, section placement and "(default ...)" suffixes for all nine flags already match. The two modifier-requires rules also work: both `--script-limit 5` and `--script-format bash` alone produce exit 1 with the correct first line `Error: --<name> requires --emit-script`. So the audit surface is narrow: argv/help/partial-validation are done; dispatch, the emitters, and the store are not.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER CAN REUSE (important, saves most of the work):
- All nine flags depend on inputs the Rust port ALREADY builds in run_robot_triage (crates/bv/src/main.rs:1097, payload assembly ~main.rs:1418-1455): the triage result, data_hash, source_authority, and the full RobotEnvelope. Do not recompute; call the same helper.
- The existing dispatch idiom to copy is the --export-md block at crates/bv/src/main.rs:91 (`args.iter().position(|a| a == "--export-md")`) or --export-graph at main.rs:118. Insert the five export/script branches there, before main.rs:494.
- bv-export (crates/bv-export/src/lib.rs) currently exposes only graph_export, mermaid, preview, hooks — a `brief` module must be added, porting pkg/export/markdown.go:718-928 (PriorityBriefConfig, DefaultPriorityBriefConfig, GeneratePriorityBriefFromTriageJSON) plus Go's generateJQHelpers() at cmd/bv/main.go:6940-7021, which is a pure static markdown string that can be copied verbatim.

THE TRAP FOR --feedback-*: do NOT touch crates/bv-correlation/src/feedback.rs. It is already a faithful port of the UNRELATED Go pkg/correlation/feedback.go — a JSONL append-only store at `<beadsDir>/correlation_feedback.jsonl` (FEEDBACK_FILE, crates/bv-correlation/src/feedback.rs:27) holding confirm/reject/ignore on correlations, used by --robot-confirm-correlation / --robot-reject-correlation / --robot-correlation-stats. The four --feedback-* flags use a completely different store: Go's pkg/analysis/feedback.go, a single pretty-printed JSON object at `.beads/feedback.json` (FeedbackFile = "feedback.json") that re-weights the scoring factors. `grep -rn 'feedback.json' --include=*.rs .` returns nothing — that store does not exist in Rust at all.

SECOND TRAP: the weight-update math is a silent no-op unless you fix the data model first. Go's updateWeightAdjustments (pkg/analysis/feedback.go:245-289) reads `breakdown.PageRankNorm` etc. — the RAW normalized contributions. Rust's ScoreBreakdown (crates/bv-analysis/src/scoring.rs:18-27) stores only the WEIGHTED values (compute_impact at scoring.rs:48-55 does `pagerank: pagerank_norm * WEIGHT_PAGE_RANK`) and drops the eight `*_norm` fields that Go's ScoreBreakdown carries alongside them (pkg/analysis/priority.go:24-42). Without adding those fields, every --feedback-accept/--feedback-ignore would "succeed" but leave weight_adjustments pinned at 1.0 forever. Go's smoothing: delta = direction * contribution * 0.1, clamp to [0.5, 2.0], then adj = 0.2*target + 0.8*old, with direction = +1 for accept and -1 for ignore.

KNOCK-ON SURFACE: the same missing store silently breaks scoring re-weighting on --robot-triage, --robot-next (robot_registry.go:2470) and --robot-priority (robot_registry.go:2470) once >=3 events exist (MinFeedbackSamples, feedback.go:310-315). Proven with a diff_robot run in a scratch dir holding 3 recorded events: 31 leaves only in GO, the entire `.feedback.*` subtree. Note Rust already PRINTS the hint `jq '.feedback.weight_adjustments' - View feedback-adjusted weights (bv-90)` at crates/bv/src/main.rs:1469 — it advertises a JSON path it never emits. Also: `--feedback-ignore` takes precedence over `--feedback-accept` when both are passed (Go main.go:2473-2477), and `--feedback-reset` is checked before `--feedback-show` and before accept/ignore (main.go:2454).

MINOR PARITY NITS worth folding in: (1) the modifier-requires recovery hint differs — Go prints a per-modifier `Try: `bv --emit-script --script-limit 5`.` (main.go:305-306 + formatModifierRecoveryExamples) where Rust prints the generic `Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)`; this affects the whole MODIFIER_REQUIRES table, not just this group. (2) Rust has NO enum-flag validation at all (crates/bv/src/validation.rs is 177 lines, containing only validate_modifier_requires + validate_exclusive_primaries), so `--emit-script --script-format sh` launches the TUI instead of exiting 1 with Go's `invalid --script-format "sh" (expected one of bash, fish, zsh); did you mean "zsh"?`. Go's enumRules covers script-format AND graph-format (main.go:1846-1848), so porting the validator should cover both.

AUDIT HYGIENE: no file in either repo was created, edited, or deleted. `--priority-brief` and `--agent-brief` were pointed at /tmp scratch paths; the four mutating `--feedback-*` flags were exercised ONLY inside an isolated copy at /tmp/scratch_bv/fbtest (a copy of .beads/issues.jsonl + metadata.json), so `.beads/feedback.json` was never created in the real repo — confirmed afterwards by `ls .beads/feedback.json` (still 'No such file or directory') and `git status --porcelain` in both repos. One caveat for the implementer's test plan: the stock ./scripts/diff_robot.sh has no per-binary timeout and WILL HANG on these flags until the TUI fallthrough is fixed. To get a printable diff during development I made a byte-identical copy at /tmp/scratch_bv/diff_robot_timed.sh that only wraps each leg in `timeout 120`; the `### args` / `### exit` / leaf-diff lines it prints are genuine script output. NOTE: rust exit code is nondeterministic (1 when stdout is a file, 124 when it times out on a TTY) — the signal to trust is the `Loaded 46 issues — launching TUI` stderr line plus the byte-count mismatch, not the specific exit code.
verifierSummary: I could not refute a single one of the nine gaps: all nine flags are declared in Rust's flag tables and consumed nowhere, all nine fall through to the TUI at crates/bv/src/main.rs:494, and I re-ran the diff for every one of them myself (own timed copy of scripts/diff_robot.sh in /tmp, all mutating flags exercised only in an isolated /tmp copy of .beads — both repos left clean, `git status --porcelain` shows only the pre-existing `?? docs/` and `.beads/feedback.json` does not exist). Rust is uniformly worse: rust=124/1 vs go=0/1, with `Loaded 46 issues — launching TUI` on stderr and TUI escape codes on stdout. Nothing here is a documented scope cut: AGENTS.md has no exemption, and the CLOSED beads p3-dispatch-3lv ("briefs/emit-script" in the mandated startup order) and p3-cli-surface-r6c ("emit-script+limit+format", "script-format enum bash|fish|zsh") put these squarely in scope. What I did refute is a set of claims in the supporting evidence and advice, four of which would send the implementer down a wrong path: (1) --priority-brief/--agent-brief — the `*Generated:` line is NOT robotNow()/SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; I proved it by running the oracle with and without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1787407612 and getting byte-identical briefs stamped with local wall-clock, so following the advice guarantees a mismatch, and the proposed `cmp` test is minute-flaky; (2) --emit-script — the claim that redirecting stdout to a file makes the TUI exit 1 is false (diff_robot.sh hangs, OUTER_EXIT=124), and the suggested "reuse the triage payload" is blocked by a real Windows bug in bv-core's lookup_path (no .exe/PATHEXT expansion -> "tracker executable is unavailable: br" -> "# No verified live tracker route" where Go emits real br commands), which must be fixed first or the port cannot be byte-identical; (3) --feedback-show — the audit's "byte-identical" acceptance criterion is impossible because the ORACLE ITSELF is nondeterministic (6 consecutive Go runs, 6 different md5s; Go's getEffectiveWeightsLocked sums a map in randomized order), so the audit's own quoted expected leaf `.feedback.effective_weights.PageRank = 0.21999999999999995` is one of several legal values; the gate must normalize that subtree; (4) --script-limit — the recovery-hint fix is per-modifier with a nil default (Go returns "" for unmapped modifiers), not a shared table addition. Minor corrections: the `.feedback` block appears in --robot-triage at >=1 event, not >=3 (only `applied`/re-weighting need 3), and the --feedback-accept/--feedback-ignore tests cannot use diff_robot.sh as-is because the Go leg mutates state the Rust leg then reads.

auditNotes:
STRUCTURAL FINDINGS FOR SIBLING AUDITORS

1. NOTHING IN THIS GROUP IS FULL PARITY. 0 of 16 flags. The only shared behaviour I could find is modifier-requires validation.

2. THE #1 CROSS-CUTTING DEFECT: unimplemented primaries fall through to the interactive TUI and block forever. Rust guards `--robot-*` primaries at crates/bv/src/main.rs:472-481 ("registered but not yet implemented") and rejects stray positionals at main.rs:487-492, but there is NO equivalent guard for the non-robot primaries. Go's hasNonRobotPrimaryArg (cmd/bv/main.go:1005-1012) lists exactly: version, help, check-update, update, update-dry-run, rollback, pages, export-pages, preview-pages, export, export-md, export-graph. In Rust, `--export` and `--pages` match nothing and reach main.rs:494. scripts/diff_robot.sh has NO timeout, so any diff run against these flags hangs the harness — every such finding in this report was measured with a /tmp wrapper (/tmp/bvcmp.sh) that is byte-identical to scripts/diff_robot.sh apart from a per-binary `timeout` and `</dev/null`. This also silently affects scripts/capture_goldens.sh and scripts/classify_goldens.sh.

3. TWO COMPLETELY UNPORTED Go PACKAGES BLOCK THIS ENTIRE GROUP. pkg/export/sqlite_export.go (36 KB) + sqlite_schema.go + vendor_assets/ and pkg/export/wizard.go (31 KB) + github.go (32 KB) + cloudflare.go (27 KB) have no Rust counterpart. `--export-pages` needs the first set, `--pages` needs the second. Both are prerequisites, not nice-to-haves.

4. THREE DEAD-BUT-PRESENT RUST MODULES. crates/bv-export/src/hooks.rs is a faithful port that nothing calls (lib.rs:8 re-exports it; no call sites exist). The livereload half of crates/bv-export/src/preview.rs is a stub: the watcher thread (preview.rs:88-95) is an empty 500 ms poll loop and `sse_clients` (preview.rs:101-103) is bound then discarded, so live reload cannot work even with the plumbing in place. And crates/bv/src/main.rs:146-149 hardcodes the graph page title/heading instead of reading --graph-title. "Ported but unwired" is the dominant failure mode in this group — grep for the module, not for the flag.

5. BOOLEAN-FLAG PARSING IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF THREE SEPARATE BUGS. crates/bv/src/argv.rs:300-323 only classifies a token as bool-vs-value-taking; it has no value parser, so every Go bool that accepts `--flag=false` is mishandled. Confirmed wrong today: --pages-include-closed (3 of 4 forms wrong), --pages-include-history (never read), --no-live-reload (value dropped), --export-include-graph (never read). A single `Option<bool>`-returning helper fixes all four. Note the inconsistency is already visible in main.rs: the --export-pages handler uses presence tests (main.rs:340-346) while the --export-graph handler uses position lookups (main.rs:119, 131-139) — neither is correct for Go semantics.

6. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH IS NOT PROPAGATED TO THE EXPORT WRITERS. Go pins every generated timestamp through robotNow() (cmd/bv/main.go:1165-1172). Rust's --export-md writes wall-clock time (2026-09-24T09:04:42Z under a pinned SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1787407612, where Go wrote 2026-08-22T14:06:52Z). Since diff_robot.sh pins this variable, any export that emits a timestamp will diff forever. Go's --export-pages also prints a wall-clock "[16:00:51]" on the "Export complete" line which is NOT epoch-pinned — so even a correct port will need that line normalised before the two binaries can be byte-compared.

7. VALIDATION-ERROR TEXT: SECOND LINE ALWAYS DIFFERS. Rust prints "Error: --X requires --Y" correctly, then substitutes the generic "Usage: bvr --robot-help  (full robot surface arrives with dispatch phase)" (crates/bv/src/main.rs:49). 1. --no-hooks -> not-applicable. The hooks ecosystem is an explicitly documented scope cut in COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md (Extended row line 142, "Extended class (never blocks release)" line 302, "Hooks (extended)" line 311, Phase 5 Extended scope line 405). I deliberately did NOT re-run it; the audit records that a Go run attempted a LIVE GitHub Pages deploy.

The watch loop is Extended scope (plan lines 142/302/312/405), but the `--as-of` guard is a genuine core gap I re-confirmed: Go exits 1 with the exact sentence, Rust exits 0 and writes a bundle. Advice corrected to "implement only the guard now, defer the loop".
4. --pages-title -> partial, but the implementation advice is materially wrong. The audit measured propagation via diff_robot.sh pointed at a single output dir; diff_robot.sh runs BOTH binaries at the same path, so Rust overwrote Go's index.html and the auditor grepped Rust's file. Measured in separate dirs, Go with --pages-title contains the title exactly ONCE in index.html, not twice: the Go h1 substitution is dead code because the pattern is `<h1 class="text-xl font-semibold">` while the real template is `<h1 class="text-lg sm:text-xl font-semibold">`.
